title: 音乐 + 图片 CD：让 CD 机只播放音乐、不播放图片内容的两种布局（接 #181）
body:
## 背景

@EMZ1 在 [#181](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/181) 里手工刻了一张 CD，内圈是音乐，外圈是图案。歌能正常放，但图案占了最后一条音轨，播到那一轨就会听到噪声。

我想把这个做进 DiscImageStudio，让图案留在盘面上，普通 CD 机照常放歌，曲目列表里也只出现音乐。两种布局都已在设计页的「音乐位置」里实现，目前默认把音乐放在外圈。布局 B（音乐在内圈）已经用程序内刻录实刻了一张盘，在 CD 机（Syitern R300）上播放正常，照片附在帖子下面；布局 A（音乐在外圈）还没刻过实盘。[Draft PR #284](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/284)

程序靠写入的数据在盘面形成明暗纹理。为了保留音乐的 PCM 样本，两种布局都把绘图区和音乐区分开。音乐输入是 44.1 kHz、16 位立体声 PCM WAV，样本原样写入，曲目末尾按需补静音，凑足整扇区和 4 秒的最短曲目长度。

## 布局 A · 音乐在外圈

盘心 → 导入区 → 图案（第 1 轨 `INDEX 00`，从 LBA 0 开始）→ 音乐（第 1 轨 `INDEX 01` 起）→ 导出区 → 盘缘

整张盘只有一个音频区段。图案写在第 1 轨的预间隙里，也就是 HTOA（Hidden Track One Audio）利用的位置。光盘目录（TOC）把第 1 轨的播放起点记在图案后面，正常播放直接从音乐开始。支持读首轨预间隙的 CD 机如果在第 1 首开头继续倒退，可能会播出响亮的噪声。能读取这个区域的抓轨软件也能读到图案数据。预间隙可能长达几十分钟，老机器能不能正常寻轨和显示时间，还得实测。

程序内刻录沿用现有的 DAO（整盘一次写入）流程。生成镜像时，用 Windows IMAPI 的 `AddSpecialPregap` 把图案放进预间隙，再逐首加入音乐。导出是一份 WAV 加一份带 `INDEX 00` 的 CUE，外部可以用 ImgBurn 或 `cdrecord -dao cuefile=disc.cue` 按整盘镜像刻录。按普通 TAO（逐轨写入）流程刻录，预间隙会写成静音。[IMAPI 文档](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/imapi2/nf-imapi2-irawcdimagecreator-addspecialpregap)

## 布局 B · 音乐在内圈

盘心 → 导入区 → 音乐（第 1 区段）→ 区段间隔 → 图案（第 2 区段，Mode 1 数据轨）→ 导出区 → 盘缘

区段顺序和 CD-Extra 一样，先音频，再数据。这里的第 2 区段写 Mode 1 数据轨，正式的 Enhanced CD 则使用 CD-ROM XA（Mode 2 Form 1）和 `CDPLUS` 目录。普通音频 CD 机通常只读第 1 区段，播放和首轨倒退都读不到第 2 区段的图案。支持多区段的电脑光驱可以读取第 2 区段的 ISO 9660 文件系统和随盘文件。[PR 的兼容性说明](https://github.com/WindowsNoEditor/DiscImageStudio/blob/264910b7ece0ce48087a405ff0f68d8bc462b8b3/docs/CD_AUDIO_COMPATIBILITY.md)

第 1 区段写完并关闭后，光驱才会报告第 2 区段的实际起点。起点差一个扇区，图案就可能转十几到三十多度。预览用预计值，程序内刻录则通过新增的 MMC 写入器走 TAO，读到实际地址后再生成并写入图片 ISO。用外部软件时，也要先刻音乐并保留追加，读出下一区段起点（例如用 `cdrecord -msinfo`），再按这个地址重新生成和刻录 ISO。两个区段之间的导出区、导入区和数据轨预间隙由光驱写入，这一圈留白。

## 两种布局怎么选

| | A · 音乐在外圈（默认） | B · 音乐在内圈 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 图案位置 | 第 1 轨预间隙 | 第 2 区段的 Mode 1 数据轨 |
| CD 机能否播到图案 | 正常从音乐开始，部分机型倒退可读到图案 | 图案在第 1 区段的音频播放范围之外 |
| 图案起点 | 固定为 LBA 0 | 以光驱报告的地址为准 |
| 区段间隔 | 单区段，没有区段间隔 | 约 11,400 扇区不能绘图，盘面上约 1 mm 宽 |
| 曲目之间 | 刻录时不额外插入 2 秒静音 | 当前 TAO 写入方式会插入 2 秒静音 |
| 随盘文件 | 不支持 | 支持 |
| 用外部软件刻录 | WAV + CUE，一次刻录 | 先刻音乐，再按实际起点生成并刻录 ISO |
| 80 分钟盘放 15 分 51 秒音乐时，绘图区占可用盘面的估算 | 约 80% | 约 77% |

我目前倾向把 A 设为默认。它沿用现有的刻录流程，图案位置在写入前就能确定。最想先确认的是，几十分钟的首轨预间隙会不会让老机器读盘变慢，以及倒退能听到噪声这件事，在实际使用里有多大影响。

## 还考虑过的做法

- 把图案接在最后一首后面（#181 的做法）。制作最简单，但图案本身会成为一条可播放的曲目。
- 把图案做成第 1 条数据轨，后面接音乐。某些老 CD 机会把混合模式盘的第一条数据轨当音频播，还是可能听到噪声。
- 用音频最低位（LSB）画图。我估算对比度只有满幅绘图的一到两成，在 CD-R 上很难看清。
- 把图案写进加长的导出区。这样能把图案留在节目区之外，能不能用现有光驱写出来还没验证过。

## 验证进度

设计页的音乐列表和面积预览、导出、程序内刻录和命令行都已实现。PR 里的回归测试已通过。布局 A 用 Windows IMAPI 生成了完整的原始镜像，并逐扇区检查了内容、地址、Q 子通道和 TOC。布局 B 的刻录命令序列先在软件模拟的 CD-R 上验证过，随后用程序内刻录实刻了一张盘：

- Syitern R300 CD 机能正常播放音乐。
- 在第 1 首开头继续按快退，机器停在 0:00，退不进图案所在的区域，也听不到噪声。
- 盘面图案的位置和方向与设计页一致，没有整体旋转或错位。

这只是一台刻录机、一张盘、一台 CD 机的结果。电脑读取第 2 区段、日志里预计起点与光驱报告起点的差值还没有记录。布局 A 还没有实盘结果。

布局 B 的这次结果已经写进 PR。布局 A 的实盘结果，以及更多机器对长预间隙和多区段盘的读盘表现，我会继续补上。[Draft PR #284](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/284)

## 想听听大家的意见

1. 你会选哪种布局做默认？A 的刻录流程更简单，B 把图案留在音频区段之外。
2. 如果你在 CD 随身听、车载 CD 或组合音响上试过很长的首轨预间隙，机器寻轨、显示时间和读盘的表现怎么样？方便的话请附上型号。
3. 两种布局都值得留吗？如果只能维护一种，你会留哪一种？
4. 还有什么办法能保留盘面图案，同时让 CD 机只播音乐？

## English summary

Draft PR #284 adds two ways to put music and a visible picture on the same CD while keeping the picture out of the track list. Layout A (the current default) puts the picture in track 1’s pre-gap and the music on the outer rings. It reuses the existing Disc-at-Once writer, and the picture’s position is fixed before burning. On players that can rewind into the pre-gap, the picture can be heard as noise.

Layout B puts the music on the inner rings in session 1 and the picture in a Mode 1 data track in session 2. It follows the audio-first, data-second layout of CD-Extra and uses a new Track-at-Once writer. About 11,400 sectors between sessions are unavailable for drawing. The writer generates the picture ISO once the recorder reports where session 2 starts.

Both layouts preserve the original PCM samples. Layout B has been burned once with the in-app writer: a Syitern R300 CD player plays the music normally, rewinding at the start of track 1 stops at 0:00, and the picture sits where the design page shows it. Layout A has not been burned to a physical disc yet. Which layout would you pick as the default? If you’ve tried discs with long track 1 pre-gaps on older players, I’d like to hear which models you tried and how they behaved.

title: 更精准的盘片预设分类系统 A More Precise Disc Preset Classification System
body: 相信各位都已注意到，即使是同一产品，批次不同也可能意味着盘片物理参数有较大的不同。这是个比较要紧的问题，我们上周也已经关注到并敲定了解决方案。但因为现实繁忙，一直拖到今天才整理并在此将内容发布出来供讨论。 As you may have noticed, even for the same product, different batches may mean that the disc's physical parameters differ considerably. This is a rather important issue. We became aware of it last week and have settled on a solution. However, due to real-life commitments, we only got around to organizing and publishing the content here for discussion today. 更改： Changes: 每套盘片预设将引入两个新的字段：**盘片媒体代码（MID）**，与盘片内圈塑料环上的**内圈代码**。 Each disc preset will introduce two new fields: the **disc media code (MID)** and the **inner-ring code** on the disc's plastic inner ring. MID可由相关API获取，为此我们推送了一个新功能：光驱信息读取。当您的电脑连接到光驱时，工程菜单栏的下方将会出现一个模块。 MID can be obtained via the relevant API. To this end, we have shipped a new feature: optical drive information reading. When your computer is connected to an optical drive, a module will appear below the project menu bar. 拥有相同MID的盘片物理参数并不相同。MID仅作与“产品名称”类似的作用，并为之后实现**检索当前插入盘片的 MID 是否有相关预设**铺路。 Discs with the same MID do not necessarily have the same physical parameters. MID serves a role similar to a "product name" and paves the way for later implementing **a check of whether there is a relevant preset for the MID of the currently inserted disc**. 而内圈代码则为分别不同批次/产线光盘起到了决定性作用，这个字段不能自动获取，必须由预设贡献者手动给出。 The inner-ring code, however, plays a decisive role in distinguishing discs from different batches/production lines. This field cannot be obtained automatically and must be provided manually by preset contributors. 需要注意，一些厂家的内圈代码还会有每一张盘片的独一无二的序列号，这个是不需要的。 Note that for some manufacturers, the inner-ring code also includes a unique serial number for each disc; this is not needed. 光驱信息读取功能将在下一个发布版本中呈现，欢迎关注。届时，我们将向已经贡献参数的贡献者们征求追加这两个字段。 The optical drive information reading feature will be available in the next release; stay tuned. At that time, we will ask contributors who have already contributed parameters to add these two fields. 在发布前的这一段时间，欢迎各位在此讨论并提出建议。 During the period before the release, everyone is welcome to discuss and offer suggestions here.

title: 数据面刻图：清明上河图，和会变色的花瓣 / Data-side pictures: the Qingming scroll, and petals that change colour
body: 两张用普通 DVD-R 刻的盘，图都在数据面（刻录的那一面），不是标签面。光驱是 HL-DT-ST GH70N，盘是 Ritek F1 DVD-R，刻录用 Windows 自带的光盘映像刻录机。 ### 清明上河图 整卷画排成内外两圈。用的是对数极坐标（共形）映射，人物和房屋在弯成圆环后还保持原来的比例；画面从内圈末尾接到外圈开头，接缝处角度对得上。原卷的引首和题跋填在首尾。 这张盘的几何参数没有拍照标定，也没有试刻：是让光驱读一张已刻好的同批盘、从读取时间推算出来的（方法见 #107）。只刻了一次，第一次就是这个样子。 ### 会变色的花瓣 每朵花的四片花瓣写的是四种不同的重复数据（`A5`、`92`、`66` 和 `ED00`）。重复的数据在轨道上排成周期性的坑，像一把很细的梳子，把光按颜色散开；梳齿间距不同，同一个角度看过去颜色就不同。所以同一朵花上能同时看到三四种颜色，转一下盘，颜色跟着变。背景是没有周期的混合数据，所以没有颜色。照片是手机闪光灯拍的。原理和测量见 #108。 ### 怎么看 彩虹般的"披萨片"是盘上导槽本身的衍射，和图无关。想看图，就拿一个小而亮的光源（比如手机闪光灯，或屏幕上一小块白色），在它的镜面反射方向附近看盘，慢慢倾斜。 工具和全部记录：[Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe) --- Two ordinary DVD-Rs with pictures on the data side (the recorded side), not the label. Drive: HL-DT-ST GH70N. Discs: Ritek F1 DVD-R. Burned with Windows' built-in disc image burner. **Along the River During the Qingming Festival.** The whole scroll on two rings, using a conformal (log-polar) mapping so people and buildings keep their proportions after bending into a ring. The painting runs from the end of the inner ring into the start of the outer ring at the same angle; the scroll's frontispiece and colophons fill the ends. The disc geometry came from read timing on another disc from the same spindle (see #107), with no photo calibration and no test burn. It was burned once, and this is that first burn. **Petals that change colour.** The four petals of each flower hold four different repeated data patterns (`A5`, `92`, `66` and `ED00`). Repeated data lays the pits out at a regular spacing along the track, like a very fine comb that spreads light into colours, and a different spacing sends a different colour towards the same viewing angle. So one flower shows three or four colours at once, and they shift as you turn the disc. The background holds a mix without any period and stays colourless. Photographed with a phone flash. Details in #108. **How to look.** The rainbow "pizza slices" come from the disc's own groove and have nothing to do with the picture. To see the picture, take a small bright light (a phone flash, or a small white patch on a screen) and look at the disc near its mirror reflection, tilting slowly. Tools and full notes: [Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe)

nodes.body: 清明上河图可以分享下吗！

@wiknzylix 可以分享一下制作思路！

原始高清扫描文件大约有3GB（）有点太大了不太好发 而且我不确定它的再分发许可，所以暂时不直接提供。不过网上可以找到其他版本的《清明上河图》，用来尝试这个方法应该没问题（）

我当时的处理方法大致如下：

1. 双环布局：将长卷沿长度方向切成左右两段，分别映射到DVD数据面的外圈和内圈。因为外圈周长更大，所以分配更长的图像。按照两个环带的中心半径计算，理论上大约是 60:40（外圈:内圈），实际切割位置可以根据画面内容调
2. 保持原始比例：先按照原图长宽比缩小，尽量避免人物和建筑被直接拉伸，再将两段分别进行极坐标映射
3. 反向畸变补偿：直接进行极坐标变换会产生明显的切向尺度差异，因为相同角度在不同半径上对应的弧长为 s = r × θ。因此需要在映射前进行反向几何预畸变，补偿外侧图案偏大、内侧图案偏小的问题
4. 接缝处理：尽量选择画面中不太重要的场景作为切割位置，再利用背景、留白和题跋填充环绕后剩余的空间，让接缝不那么突兀

另外需要说明一下：我这张光盘是按约 2 μm 的空间精度制作的。 当前 DiscImageStudio 的常规刻录流程无法直接达到这个精度，因此实际使用了我自己编写的 ISO 生成脚本，这部分代码目前没有公开

所以以上主要是图像排版和几何变换的思路。如果只想尝试类似的视觉效果，可以先用普通高清版本和 DIS 进行低分辨率复现，不一定需要原始的 3 GB 扫描文件![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/458db0a6-f3d2-4285-baa9-6e209b1efda6)

title: HoloStudio3D: an experimental 3D hologram add-on built on Disc Image Studio
body: Hi! I built HoloStudio3D, an experimental add-on for Disc Image Studio that burns 3D “hologram” pictures into DVDs from pictures, depth maps or 3D models. It uses DVD data patterns as diffraction gratings, so each eye sees a different view. It also includes an English edition of Disc Image Studio and uses disc-probe to measure discs. https://github.com/drewmedina55-ux/HoloStudio3D Huge thanks to JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat and all the Disc Image Studio contributors. This wouldn’t exist without your work. It’s GPL-3.0 and fully credited. Feedback and test burns are very welcome! Thank you again so much for creating this tech, It is amazing and I can't wait to see where it goes! - Drew 我基于 Disc Image Studio 做了一个实验性的 3D 全息光盘插件 HoloStudio3D，非常感谢作者和所有贡献者！欢迎试用和反馈。

title: 我正在尝试为DIS添加允许 DVD+RW 直接刻录至光盘功能
body:
项目地址:https://github.com/Doctor-shengru/DiscImageStudio/tree/feature/dvd-rw-overwrite
## What this fixes

Fixes #203.

A DVD+RW never returns to IMAPI's `BLANK` state (0x2) after its first format:
erasing only replaces the disc contents, so `IDiscFormat2Data` keeps reporting
`IMAPI_FORMAT2_DATA_MEDIA_STATE_OVERWRITE_ONLY` (0x1). Such a disc is empty
(`FreeSectorsOnMedia` = 2,295,104 = the whole data area, `MediaHeuristicallyBlank=True`,
`MediaPhysicallyBlank=False`), yet every later streaming burn stops at
"DVD 不是空白盘，已取消刻录".

Relaxing the blank check alone would not fix it: `IDiscFormat2Data::Write` refuses
non-blank media with `E_IMAPI_DF2DATA_MEDIA_NOT_BLANK` (0xC0AA0405) unless
`IDiscFormat2Data::ForceOverwrite` is `VARIANT_TRUE`. The request therefore has to
carry the user's explicit permission to overwrite.

## Changes

- `OpticalBurnRequest.OverwriteRewritableMedia` (default `false`).
- Burn page gains a DVD-only checkbox, off by default
  ("允许覆写已写入的 DVD±RW（整盘擦除）"), a hint below it, and a different
  confirmation text that states the old contents are erased.
- `BurnData` reads `TotalSectorsOnMedia`, derives `overwrite` from the request flag
  and the media state, and passes it to `ConfigureMedia`, which sets `ForceOverwrite`.
- `ValidateWritableDataCapacity` accepts a non-blank disc only when the option is on
  and IMAPI reports `OVERWRITE_ONLY`. Appendable and finalized write-once media still
  throw, with a message naming the limitation.
- When overwriting, the capacity check uses the disc total because the rewrite starts
  at LBA 0; `ReadDvdMediaCapacity` reports the total for an overwrite-only disc.
- DVD diagnostics print `TotalSectors=` and `Overwrite=`; the existing
  `ForceOverwrite=` device setting is unchanged.

## Validation

- `dotnet build DiscImageStudio.slnx --configuration Release`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `dotnet run --project tests/DiscImageStudio.ArchitectureTests --configuration Release`:
  all suites pass, including the new `dvd-rewritable-overwrite` suite (blank path,
  opt-in, total-capacity bound, write-once rejection, capacity reporting).
- `dotnet run --project src/DvdImageSolver --configuration Release -- selftest`: passed.
- **No physical overwrite burn has been recorded yet.** The change was developed on a
  MATSHITA DVD+-RW UJ8B1 (firmware D.03) with a RITEK DVD+RW whose log is in #203;
  the author will post the first real burn result (pattern position and read-back)
  here before this leaves draft.

## Test plan on real hardware

1. Insert a used/erased DVD+RW, open 刻录, select the DVD project, tick
   "允许覆写已写入的 DVD±RW".
2. The log must show `MediaState=0x00000001`, `Overwrite=True`, `ForceOverwrite=True`,
   and the burn must start instead of failing with "不是空白盘".
3. Check the drawing's position and orientation on the disc and compare with the
   read-back preview; a wrong start LBA would show as a shifted or wrapped drawing.


目前遇到的问题，手中DVD+RW尚未完成标定，无法判断偏差，但初步判断偏差与未校订的偏差大致一致
故希望有DVD+RW且完成标定的能帮忙跑一下验证

title: 有没有做好的参数
body: 同一个品牌的同一型号光盘参数能通用吗？还是说和使用的光驱也有关系，换一个光驱就需要重新标定参数吗？

nodes.body:
简单说，参数主要跟盘走。换光驱对 DVD 影响不大，同品牌同型号的盘却不一定通用。下面是我们和几位用户测到的，样本都不多。

**同品牌同型号不一定通用：**

- 三组 Verbatim DVD+R 参数（#74、#140 和内置的 `verbatim-dvd-plus-r-azo-43498`），内外半径只差几 µm，换算成转角后，在 25.8 到 54.5 mm 之间差了约 300° 到 870°。这几组盘的批次不一定相同，但可以看出半径看着接近不代表能用。
- bczhc 在 #67 里，同一次买的盘中有一张内环编码不同，标定结果也不一样。
- #127 的 Thinkplus 扇区数和别人不同，用别人的参数差得很远；#109 也有人反馈匹配不上。
- 我们测过两张 MID 都是 `CMC MAG. AM3` 的盘，轨距差约 0.7%。

所以可以先比三样：MID、扇区数（DIS 的“从光盘读取”）、内环的编码。都一样才比较有把握，只看包装不够。

**换光驱：**

DVD 上目前看一般不用重新标定。bczhc 用照片标定的参数，和我们用另一台光驱（GH70N）读取计时测的同种盘，全盘相差在 0.04° 以内；笔记本光驱 PLDS DS8A8SH 和 GH70N 相差约 0.05° rms。轨道是盘出厂时压好的导槽，刻录机是跟着导槽走的，这可能就是原因。

CD 我们的数据还太少。读取计时测的结果在不同光驱上要另外确认一个沿轨道常数（我们见过约 206 帧和约 7 帧）。用照片标定的 CD 参数换刻录机能不能通用，我们没有测过。
谢谢，我已经弄好了，感觉教程还是不够简洁，明天我整理个傻瓜版的出来，4张盘就能把精读校的挺高了

title: 经验分享：一种极粗标定方法，适用于粗标定也无法工作的场景
body: 如题，在光盘实际几何与初始设定值相差极远的情况下，粗标定方法无法产生有效结果，因此我摸索出了一种能快速地在几轮内就收敛到可直接使用边界标定进行校准的流程，与 Issue #185 的标定流程是类似的。 ## 基本原理 1. 当 **设定几何** 的内半径比 **实际几何** 的内半径 **小** 时，内圈的图案会向一个方向偏移 2. 当 **设定几何** 的外半径比 **实际几何** 的外半径 **大** 时，外圈的图案会向**另**一个方向偏移 3. 因此，人为设定一个特别初始值，比如对于12cm碟片设定内半径为24mm，外半径为60mm，可认为必定能得出一张中间某处有明显折返点的刻录结果 ## 准备 以一张未标定的12cm盘为例，使用一张半白半黑图，如下 然后设定初始几何设定值为内半径24mm，外半径60mm，开始标定流程 ## 流程 以当前配置刻录出一张盘，随后观察一道非常明显的空白间隔，如图： 可以观察到，此时这条间隔很窄但足够明显，因此可以大刀阔斧地收紧内外半径范围，比如这里我收紧到了25-59，得出下一轮结果： 此后再重复几次这个流程，得到几乎没有圈而是大块色块（类似边界标定那样）时，就可以进入边界标定流程了

nodes.body:
谢谢分享！用半黑半白图找折返点这个思路很直观，几轮就能从差得很远收敛到能做边界标定，对粗标定跑不动的盘很有用 (๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧

我补充另一条路，也适合“初始值差得很远”的情况：不看图，让光驱自己量。我们做了个小工具 [disc-probe](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe)，原理是读盘计时。光驱读完一个扇区的时刻，对应盘正转到哪个角度。在盘上很多位置这样读，就能直接算出这张盘的内半径和轨距（相邻两圈轨道之间的距离）。它不需要初始值，所以差多远都一样。

我们这边的结果：

- 刻一张写满随机数据的盘，测完用测出的参数刻网格图，不做任何修正，网格线的角度误差峰峰值 0.106°（GH70N 光驱，铼德 RITEKF1 DVD-R）。
- 同一桶的两张盘测出来只差 0.12 到 0.17°，所以同一桶测一张就够。
- 今天还试了只用一张盘：内圈先刻一半随机数据，测完不封盘，外圈接着刻网格。肉眼看是直的，扫描量化还在做。

也说一下限制，免得说过头：

- 要光驱支持。有的光驱计时不稳，或者读取方式特殊，测不出来。我们在 [#107](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/107) 收集各型号的实测情况。
- 测量范围以外（最外圈几毫米）是推算的。有一台 GP65NB60 已经测到 58 mm，外圈的线还是有点卷，原因还在查。
- 刻盘验证到这个精度的，目前主要是 GH70N。别的光驱有测量结果，但刻盘验证还少。

所以两种方法可以互补：光驱能计时，就先测一张，大概率一次就到位；不能计时，或者想最后确认一下，就用你这种看图的方法。

<details>
<summary>具体怎么做</summary>

1. 生成随机数据镜像并刻录：`python -m discprobe random --output iso/random.iso`
2. 把刻好的盘放回光驱测量：`python -m discprobe geo --drive E:`（E: 换成你的光驱）
3. 测完它会提示下一步的命令，包括导出给 DiscImageStudio 用的预设。不确定走到哪一步了，可以运行 `python -m discprobe guide` 查看。

详细步骤见仓库里的 `docs/MANUAL.md`。

</details>
感谢大佬做的工具qwq，我就是这种粗标也一团糊糊的情况，比上面的图还糟糕完全看不出来任何纹路，用了disc probe就直接跳到细标了

@MissPinkElfLady 太好了，能帮上忙真开心 (๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧

@taniyareece7329-create 没有单个 exe，不过有一个开箱即用的 Windows 包，效果差不多：

1. 到 [Releases](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/releases/latest) 下载 `disc-probe-0.1.1-full-win64.zip`（61 MB）。
2. 解压到任意文件夹。
3. 双击里面的 `开始 Start.bat`，会打开一个命令窗口，按提示一步步走就行。

包里自带 Python 和需要的库，不用另外安装任何东西，删掉文件夹就等于卸载。不方便用管理员身份运行的话，在读光驱的命令后面加 `--transport imapi`。

title: 威宝 BD-RE 43614 没有图案
body: 我手上的这个盘，很怪异。按说对于任何一个未校准盘，如果使用了标靶图像，刻录出来应该能显示那些环，只不过四条径向线可能会被扭曲乃至完全看不见。但我这个BD-RE，使用一个预设参数做出标靶刻出来竟然，连环都看不到。就是那种像是纯随机的数据而已。盘面上任何一丁点明暗特征都不能见到。这是盘的问题吗？我不知道该如何进行下一步了。包括DIS软件里的粗调图案，刻出来也是什么看不到。

nodes.body: https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/210 这里有一张同MID的盘。然而我用那边的参数，刻标靶文件，就是什么都无，连环都无。这是有可能的嘛
用这样的图也看不到任何特征

哦！我终于是解决了！是备用区的问题。

我其实之前就想过会不会是备用区的问题，因为`cdrskin -minfo`查看的扇区数是11826176而非12219392，网上查了[一下](https://forum.imgburn.com/topic/19958-bd-r-12219392-sectors-versus-11826176/)这两个值，就说蓝光盘留给用户的是11826176扇区数，剩下的是作为备用区进行缺陷管理用的。但我并没在意。我看备用区是在光盘最外圈，按理那就不会影响到里面，从头写反正都是一样。但其实并不是。问了下AI，这玩意当开启了缺陷管理时，里面也有块区域要用来存放信息，所以用户数据就继续往外放了，造成PSN偏移，于是就影响了反扰码算法，就全乱了。

我最开始使用的是`dvd+rw-format`格式化，它就自动开启了缺陷管理。光盘在保留了备用区状态后写入时做调整是无济于事的。我之前给`cdrskin`开了`stream_recording=on`，这样只能保证在写入时不回读（从而稳定2x，否则只有1x速），但PSN偏移还在。解决方法，必须要给BD-RE重新格式化一遍以关掉备用区。

先list出光盘支持的格式化选项。
```
❯ cdrskin -v dev=/dev/sr1 --list_formats                                             12:01:32
cdrskin 1.5.8 : limited cdrecord compatibility wrapper for libburn
cdrskin: verbosity level : 1
cdrskin: NOTE : greying out all drives besides given dev='/dev/sr1'
cdrskin: scanning for devices ...
cdrskin: ... scanning for devices done
Media current: BD-RE
Format status: formatted, with 23866.0 MiB
BD Spare Area: 0 blocks consumed, 0 blocks available
Format idx 0 : 00h , 11826176s , 23098.0 MiB
Format idx 1 : 30h , 11826176s , 23098.0 MiB
Format idx 2 : 30h , 11564032s , 22586.0 MiB
Format idx 3 : 30h , 12088320s , 23610.0 MiB
Format idx 4 : 31h , 12219392s , 23866.0 MiB
```

一定要使用第四个。然后
```bash
cdrskin -v dev=/dev/sr1 blank=format_by_index_4
``` 

这个项目文档里倒是提到了需要无备用区来刻录，但我不知如何操作。搞半天才知道`cdrskin`能支持多个格式化选项。而且只有BD-RE跟DVD-RAM在硬件上就设计有备用区和缺陷管理这个东西，DVD-RW DVD+RW CD-RW都是没有的，这也就解释了为何我手上的那些光盘都没踩到这个坑。

title: 透明区域存放其他数据
body:
一种简单的方法。把要放的数据中的0x9b 0x92 0xa5这些字节转义掉然后直接Q域填充那些非0x9b 0x92 0xa5字节区域就行了，基本就对应着图片上的透明区域。

https://github.com/bczhc/dvd-tools/tree/master/src

测试和使用方法：

```bash
# 生成艺术图ISO
disc-image-studio solve ........ --iso-output /tmp/dis.iso
# 改一些字节，把DSV平衡
target/release/dsv-balancer run /tmp/dis.iso /tmp/dis-dsv-ok.iso
# 放数据
target/release/dvd-embed embed /tmp/dis-dsv-ok.iso ~/其他数据.tar /tmp/dvd.iso
# 烧录
cdrskin -v -data /tmp/dvd.iso
# 弹出再插入
eject
# 回读盘镜像
pv /dev/sr0 > /tmp/dvd-read.iso
# 提取数据
target/release/dvd-embed extract /tmp/dvd-read.iso /tmp/extracted.tar
# 两者应当一样。
cmp ~/其他数据.tar /tmp/extracted.tar # exit -> 0
```

流式提取：

```bash
cargo run -r --bin dvd-embed extract /dev/sr0 | tar -xv
```

title: 【早期结果】在普通 DVD-R 上，让图案按设计的角度亮起来：O/X 切换、亮点合成环、红色点缀 / [Early result] Making parts of a picture light up at a chosen angle on an ordinary DVD-R: an O/X switch, spots that merge into a ring, red accents
body:
这张盘上同一个位置画了 O 和 X。手机在一个位置时亮的是 O，移动几厘米后换成 X。 两张都是同一张普通 DVD-R 的手机闪光灯照片，只做了透视校正，没有调亮。O 亮时比 X 亮 8 到 9 倍，X 亮时比 O 亮约 3 倍。 上面是手机慢慢移动时拍的 8 张连起来的效果：右边和左下的亮带朝相反方向走，右下两个亮点连起来再开成一个环。 最抢眼的其实是那两个亮点。下面四张是同一块地方，手机往一个方向移动：两个点，长大，连成花生，最后只剩外面一圈。 这段是转动盘时拍的。它和下面标了“调色”的照片都调过颜色，只是为了看得更清楚；文中的数字都来自没调色的原片。 这是一台光驱、一种盘、一部手机的早期结果，局限都写在后面。 ## 和盘上本来的彩虹有什么不同 光盘本来就有彩虹，普通刻图也会出彩虹，还常常很好看。这里用的也是同样的光学现象，不是颜料。 普通刻图里，颜色主要取决于位置和角度，彩虹带从盘心散开，图案在上面挡出形状。这张盘是先定下“手机大概在哪”，再给每一小块单独挑写法，决定它在手机到哪个位置时把光送进镜头。所以亮起来的形状跟着我们画的图走，不跟着彩虹带走。 DiscImageStudio 刻的图也会出现局部和周围不同色，甚至明暗反转，这是两种写法随角度表现不同带来的。它的界面里目前没有指定颜色的选项。我们在讨论区和仓库里没找到别人按颜色设计的做法，但这只是没找到。[#108](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/108) 里转来的小红书视频，至今不知道是不是有意设计的配色。 ## 一张人物盘 同样的办法也用在了一张人物图上，红色的鞋、臂章和下摆，蓝色的下摆和袖标。这张盘上不存数据。 左边是最初的设计图。中间是实际刻录的图案：灰度在盘上不够明显，所以我们把背景改成实底，卫衣提到最亮，黑裤和头发加了亮边，外圈的方块用来定位和测量。右边是我们搭的模拟器按中间这张算出的效果，用来模仿理想拍摄条件下的样子：亮度和颜色来自测试盘的实测，整张调亮了 2.5 倍方便看，红蓝点缀的颜色还是理论值。 模拟器只能看大致样子。它预测的亮暗差约 2 倍，实拍是 4 到 5 倍；顶部和底部的亮线、盘面反光也没有算进去。下面是实拍： 左边是这次的结果，右边是上一版（同一张图，存了数据，拍摄距离也不同）。卫衣和背景的亮暗差从约 1.2 倍提高到 4 到 5 倍，这是在手机接近设计位置时测的。 下面是调色后的几张，手机在不同位置，颜色和明暗都跟着变： 上面左边的动图没有调色。 做到的和没做到的都很明显： - 红色在设计位置接近红色，手机差约 1 cm 就可能变橙或变绿。 - 蓝色暗得多，偏蓝紫或洋红。 - 卫衣上的粉绿色带不是我们选的颜色，是纹路本身带来的。 - 左边的脸能看出轮廓和眼睛，右边的脸很弱。 所以说“选颜色”还太早。更准确的说法是：能决定一块地方在哪个角度亮，亮的时候大致是什么颜色。 ## 怎么做的 1. 先刻一张测试盘，上面是 32 种写法，每种一圈。 2. 手机沿一条线移动拍 20 多张，直接量出每种写法在不同角度有多亮、什么颜色。 3. 用这些实测结果挑写法，再刻真正的图。 一开始我们靠理论模型来挑，它预测的反差比实际高 2 到 3 倍，所以改成了先测。挑写法时用一半照片，另一半照片用来核对，避免把偶然的结果当真。 O/X 和反向流光的思路来自请 GPT 做的一份调研，那份调研是纯计算，这次是第一次实刻验证。 ## 结果 事先写好了通过标准，再刻盘拍照： | 效果 | 结果 | 通过吗 | |---|---|---| | 反向流光 | 手机移动约 4 cm，两条亮带各走约 16 mm，方向相反 | 通过 | | O/X（20 mm） | O 亮时 8 到 9 倍，X 亮时约 3 倍 | 通过 | | 两个亮点合成环 | 两点、连接、开环，顺序对 | 通过，有一档亮度阈值有噪声 | | 小 O（12、8 mm） | 约 4 倍 | 看得出形状 | | 小 X（12、8 mm） | 最高约 1.7 倍 | 没过 | | 弯道上跑的光 | 亮段单调移动，约跑了路径的 46% | 差一点 | 这次盘放歪了约 13°，手机没有走到小 X 和弯道设计的位置，所以这两项还不能算设计失败，要摆正再试。 ## 局限 - 只在一个位置附近好看。这张盘的效果靠手机位置，换个位置就是另一幅样子，这既是特点也是限制。 - 只试了一台光驱（GH70N）、一种盘（RITEKF1 DVD-R）、一部手机（iPhone 17 Pro）。别的盘和光驱，很可能要重新测一遍。 - 盘上不存数据。这几张是专门为了画面做的。 - 肉眼没有量化过，数字都来自手机照片的线性亮度，手机自己的处理也算在里面。 - 背景选得不够好：这次的背景字节在某些角度有很强的彩色辐条，照片顶部和底部能看到。好看，但不干净。 - 程序还没发布，混着私人脚本，想先整理。 很想知道有没有人试过类似的东西，或者手上的盘是不是也有这种表现。
具体实现 机位：主摄在盘心正上方 330 mm，朝图上方偏 70 mm，闪光灯相对镜头 (-43.66, +19.79) mm。这是 iPhone 17 Pro 的图纸值，用亮线方向反解，所有照片的方向误差约 1°。每张照片的机位从 ArUco 标定板解出，焦距取 EXIF。 下面的 δ 是（到灯的单位向量 + 到相机的单位向量）在轨道切向上的分量。一阶衍射满足 λ = P·δ，P 是沿轨周期。 **测试盘。** 32 个同心环，半径 24.6 到 55 mm，每环约 1 mm。候选字节由完整 ECC 和 EFMPlus 编码的频谱预测筛出。盘转到哪个方向都不影响，因为每环绕一圈。照片算出每环在 δ 上的线性 RGB。按字节混合的两环证实亮度约等于各字节的平均。 **人物盘。** 暗部全用 `A5`。亮部按 δ 每 0.05 一档，选两字节按 16 字节交替，例如 δ 0.30–0.35 用 `2D`+`8D`，δ 0.40–0.45 用 `FD`+`50`。设计时要求相邻档也不能太暗，所以窄峰的纹理（比如 `92`）被排除了。彩色点缀用周期纹路表，单元径向 0.06 mm，切向 0.057°。 **效果盘。** 给每一小格定一个“手机到 y mm 时亮”，算出那里的 δ，再选 P = 0.55 µm / δ 最接近的周期纹路。背景是字节 `00`。 | 区域 | 位置（图上角度，半径） | 手机 y（mm） | |---|---|---| | 反向流光 A | -30 到 -3°，29–53 mm | 55 → 100，随半径增大 | | 反向流光 B | 183 到 210°，29–53 mm | 100 → 55 | | 大 O / X | 20°，r 40 mm，20 mm 宽，笔画 3.5 mm | 55 / 90 | | 小 O / X | 218°，r 34、47 mm，12、8 mm 宽 | 70 / 100 | | 弯道 | 38 到 62°，r 约 41 mm | 80 → 105 | | 两团合一 | -47°，r 41 mm，Cassini 场 | 72 + 28ρ | **实测响应。** 纯周期纹路的亮峰半高宽 δ 约 0.08，是我们模型（约 0.04）的两倍。峰值约为背景的 4 到 7 倍。所以白光下独立画面的通道比模型算的少，我估计约 2 个。 **红绿蓝。** 周期纹路扇区给出，在同一 δ 下各色用不同周期时，要等量 RGB 的面积比约为： | δ | 红 | 绿 | 蓝 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 0.35 | 18% | 30% | 52% | | 0.40 | 15% | 47% | 38% | | 0.45 | 34% | 19% | 47% | | 0.50 | 19% | 32% | 48% | 长周期明显更亮：同样显蓝，P = 1.76 µm 蓝通道约 0.25，P = 1.0–1.16 µm 约 0.06–0.11。这些是手机通道，不是人眼，而且 δ 0.25–0.30 解不出可靠的比例。 读回：人物盘和效果盘全盘均匀抽 96 个 ECC 块，全部一致。测试盘每环抽 3 块，96 块里 2 块读错误，没有内容不一致。
--- **English** This disc has an O and an X drawn in the same place. With the phone in one spot the O lights up, and a few centimetres further along it's the X. Both are phone flash photos of one ordinary DVD-R, corrected for perspective and not brightened. When the O is lit it's 8 to 9 times brighter than the X, and when the X is lit it's about 3 times brighter than the O. That's 8 photos taken while moving the phone slowly. The bands on the right and lower left travel in opposite directions, and the two spots at lower right join and open into a ring. The two spots are what catches the eye most. These four show the same patch as the phone moves one way: two points, growing, joining into a peanut, then only the outer ring left. This one was taken while turning the disc. It and the photos marked as tuned below had their colours adjusted, just to make them easier to see. All the numbers here come from the untouched originals. This is an early result from one drive, one kind of disc and one phone. The limits are listed below. ## How this differs from the rainbow every disc has Discs make rainbows anyway, and ordinary pictures often look great because of it. This is the same optics, not paint. In an ordinary picture the colour mostly depends on where you are and the angle, with bands fanning out from the centre and the picture blocking out shapes on top. Here we start from roughly where the phone will be, and pick the writing for each small patch so that it sends light to the lens with the phone at a chosen spot. So the shape that lights up follows the drawing, not the rainbow bands. Pictures from DiscImageStudio can also show parts that differ in colour from their surroundings, even reversing light and dark, because its two textures behave differently with angle. Its interface doesn't currently have an option for choosing a colour. We didn't find anyone else designing by colour in the discussions or the repository, but that only means we didn't find it. We still don't know whether the Xiaohongshu video shared in [#108](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/108) used a deliberate palette. ## A disc with figures on it We used the same method on a picture of two figures, with red shoes, armband and hem, and blue on the other figure. This disc holds no data. Left is the first design. In the middle is the pattern actually burned: the greys weren't strong enough on the disc, so the background became a solid dark, the hoodie went to full bright, and the black legs and hair got a bright edge. The blocks around the edge are for locating and measuring. Right is what a simulator we built works out from the middle one, imitating how it should look when photographed under ideal conditions. Its brightness and colours come from measurements of the test disc, it's brightened 2.5 times to make it easier to see, and the red and blue accents' colours are still theoretical. The simulator only gives a rough idea. It predicted about 2 times between light and dark, where the photos reach 4 to 5 times, and it leaves out the bright lines at the top and bottom and reflections off the disc. Here are the photos: Left is this result. Right is the previous version (same picture, with data stored, taken from a different distance). The difference between the hoodie and the background went from about 1.2 times to 4 to 5 times, measured with the phone close to the designed spot. Here are some tuned photos with the phone in different places, where colour and brightness both change: The animation at the top left isn't tuned. What worked and what didn't is easy to see: - The red is close to red at the designed spot. Moving the phone about 1 cm can turn it orange or green. - The blue is much darker and leans violet or magenta. - We didn't choose the pink and green bands on the hoodie. They come from the textures. - The left face shows its outline and eyes. The right face is weak. So it's too early to say we can choose colours. What we can do is decide at which angle a patch lights up, and roughly what colour it is when it does. ## How it was made 1. Burn a test disc with 32 kinds of writing, one ring each. 2. Move the phone along a line, take 20 or so photos, and measure how bright each kind is and what colour, at each angle. 3. Pick the writing from those measurements and burn the real picture. We started out picking from a theoretical model, which predicted 2 to 3 times more contrast than we got, so we switched to measuring first. We picked on half of the photos and checked on the other half, so that a lucky result wouldn't count. The O/X and opposing bands came from a study we asked GPT to do. That study was calculation only, and this is the first time they've been burned. ## Results We wrote the pass marks down before burning: | Effect | Result | Passed? | |---|---|---| | Opposing bands | Phone moved about 4 cm, the bands moved about 16 mm each, in opposite directions | Yes | | O/X (20 mm) | 8 to 9 times when the O is lit, about 3 times when the X is lit | Yes | | Two spots into a ring | Two spots, joined, opened, in that order | Yes, with some noise at one brightness threshold | | Small O (12, 8 mm) | About 4 times | The shape can be seen | | Small X (12, 8 mm) | About 1.7 times at best | No | | Light running along a curve | Moves steadily, about 46% of the path | Just short | The disc sat about 13° off this time, so the phone never reached the spots the small X and the curve were designed for. Those two aren't design failures yet, and need another try with the disc straight. ## Limits - It only looks like this near one position. That's the point of it, and also the catch. - One drive (GH70N), one kind of disc (RITEKF1 DVD-R), one phone (iPhone 17 Pro). Other discs and drives will probably need measuring again. - These discs hold no data. They're made for the picture. - Nothing was measured by eye. All the numbers are linear brightness from phone photos, including whatever the phone does to them. - The background wasn't a great choice. That byte throws strong coloured spokes at some angles, which you can see at the top and bottom of the photos. They look nice, but it isn't clean. - The code isn't published yet. It's mixed in with private scripts and needs tidying first. If you've tried anything like this, or your discs behave this way too, I'd really like to hear about it.
Details Pose: main lens 330 mm above the disc centre and 70 mm towards the top of the picture, flash at (-43.66, +19.79) mm from the lens. That's the iPhone 17 Pro drawing's value, and the streak direction across all photos agrees to about 1°. Each photo's pose comes from an ArUco board, with the focal length from EXIF. δ below is the component along the track of (unit vector to the light + unit vector to the camera). The first order follows λ = P·δ, with P the period along the track. **Test disc.** 32 rings from radius 24.6 to 55 mm, about 1 mm each. Candidate bytes were shortlisted from spectra of fully encoded ECC and EFMPlus blocks. Rotation doesn't matter since each ring goes all the way round. Photos give linear RGB against δ for each ring. Two rings mixing bytes confirmed that brightness is close to the average of the bytes. **Figure disc.** Dark parts are all `A5`. Bright parts use two bytes alternating every 16 bytes, chosen per 0.05 of δ, such as `2D`+`8D` for δ 0.30–0.35 and `FD`+`50` for δ 0.40–0.45. A pick had to stay bright in the neighbouring bands as well, which rules out narrow peaks like `92`. Accents use periodic textures. Cells are 0.06 mm radially and 0.057° along the track. **Effects disc.** Each cell gets "light up when the phone is at y mm". That gives δ there, and we take the periodic texture closest to P = 0.55 µm / δ. The background is byte `00`. | Region | Where (angle in the picture, radius) | Phone y (mm) | |---|---|---| | Band A | -30 to -3°, 29–53 mm | 55 → 100, growing with radius | | Band B | 183 to 210°, 29–53 mm | 100 → 55 | | Big O / X | 20°, r 40 mm, 20 mm wide, strokes 3.5 mm | 55 / 90 | | Small O / X | 218°, r 34 and 47 mm, 12 and 8 mm wide | 70 / 100 | | Curve | 38 to 62°, r about 41 mm | 80 → 105 | | Two spots | -47°, r 41 mm, Cassini field | 72 + 28ρ | **Measured response.** Pure periodic textures have a peak about 0.08 wide in δ at half height, twice our model's 0.04, and reach 4 to 7 times the background. So white light offers fewer independent images than the model suggested, about 2 by my estimate. **Red, green, blue.** With a different period for each colour at the same δ, the arc sector gives these area shares for equal RGB: | δ | Red | Green | Blue | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 0.35 | 18% | 30% | 52% | | 0.40 | 15% | 47% | 38% | | 0.45 | 34% | 19% | 47% | | 0.50 | 19% | 32% | 48% | Longer periods are clearly brighter: for blue, P = 1.76 µm reaches about 0.25 and P = 1.0–1.16 µm about 0.06–0.11. These are phone channels, not the eye, and δ 0.25–0.30 didn't give reliable shares. Readback: 96 ECC blocks sampled evenly across each of the figure and effects discs, all identical. On the test disc, 3 blocks per ring, 2 of 96 had read errors and none differed.

title: 求助，为什么刻录DVD-R的时候中间会报错
body: 可以正常刻CD-R，但是DVD-R一直在失败，用ai也没查出是为什么。并且可以正常录其他ISO进去，我中间刻录了一个视频文件都是可以读取的完全没问题。 而且有好多次都是失败在一摸一样的位置，不清楚是什么情况

nodes.body: 要不试试生成镜像后用imgburn刻？
我这边在+R和-R上出现了一样的问题，最后换了两种牒，根据imgburn报错记录推出来的结论是USB线供电不足，导致无法持续让光驱进行这么高强度的烧录工作，我明天准备找更多光驱做对比测试。我现在手上的光驱USB线是USB2.0，你那边的线是什么？
我同时在使用DELL台式机自带的笔记本光驱、我的服务器上的笔记本光驱和借来的USB2.0移动光驱（HLDS的，MINI口），都没有出现过这个问题，你可以试试降低刻录速度？

> 我同时在使用DELL台式机自带的笔记本光驱、我的服务器上的笔记本光驱和借来的USB2.0移动光驱（HLDS的，MINI口），都没有出现过这个问题，你可以试试降低刻录速度？

我目前是直接用软件降到3x都会在刻入特定大小后报和该帖同样的错误，换成imgburn能刻的更多点但也无法全部完成，3x/4x/6x/8x都试过了
。同样也是刻录了一个视频文件测试是完全正常的，目前换了两种牒（杂牌/威宝）十几张了都是同样症状，只能根据报错日志推测是我手头上这个光驱的USB线供电无法应对刻录图案的工作强度。
那只能试试供电更稳定的了（也有可能是光驱内部供电不太好），因为理论上这种刻图的会有更大的瞬时功率

> 那只能试试供电更稳定的了（也有可能是光驱内部供电不太好），因为理论上这种刻图的会有更大的瞬时功率

嗯，明天我看能不能找到更多光驱后再对比试试吧~
已通过换新光驱+将旧光驱在其他电脑上进行刻录来确认，确实是光驱供电不稳定的问题，似乎只能换光驱了。
我已经换光驱了但还是一摸一样，找不到啥原因，cd一切正常DVD一张都刻不出来

> 我已经换光驱了但还是一摸一样，找不到啥原因，cd一切正常DVD一张都刻不出来

我这边新的光驱USB线是一体式的，也就是只留下USB插头，没有让线和光驱分体的设计。此外，需要把线直接插到主板的USB口中，不要插到前置USB口中。

我使用外接式的ASUS雙USB光驅，接電腦前面板，會出錯。後來發現應該是供電不穩定。
接著我使用2009年的桌機光驅，使用12V+SATA，就行了!
可能因為是USB的供電不足以讓光驅全時最大功率運轉

title: 【早期结果】图案本身就存着数据：一张 DVD-R 上的玫瑰图，同时存了 1.38 GB，整盘读回零错误 / [Early result] The picture itself holds the data: a rose picture on a DVD-R with 1.38 GB stored in it, read back with no errors
body:
想让一张盘上既有图又有文件，我们见过的做法都是给文件单独留位置：放在内圈或外圈，放在图的空白处（[#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96)），或者放到双层盘的另一层（[#59](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/59)）。刻图的地方只负责显示图案。 这张盘不分开放：图案区里约七成的地方，本身既是画面也存着数据，一共 1.38 GB，约为一张普通 DVD 容量的三成。整张盘读回来零错误，存进去的数据全部原样恢复。盘上还存了 3 份原图，也都完整恢复了。 这是用一张盘、一台光驱做的早期结果，局限都写在后面。 左边是照片，中间是刻录用的设计图，右边是这张盘上哪里存了数据。绿色的地方存着数据：玫瑰的暗部，以及上下两块只有明暗的区域。带颜色的小格和外圈彩虹边不存数据。图案区里约七成的地方带数据。照片里的颜色是另一项实验，单独写在 [#168](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/168)。 ## 图和数据怎么放在一起 就像写一句话时可以在同义词之间挑一个：意思不变，但挑了哪个词，本身就可以是暗号。 在光盘上也一样。让一块地方显得暗，有很多种写法，看起来差不多。我们挑了 16 种暗的写法和 16 种亮的写法。从 16 种里选一种，相当于每个字节藏 4 bit。 所以明暗基本不变，数据就藏在“选了哪一种”里。读的时候，光驱照常读盘，再由一个小程序把这些选择翻译回原来的数据。 ## 能存多少 | 这张盘 | 实测 1.38 GB | |---|---| | 同样的做法，不做彩色，保留彩虹边 | 约 1.97 GB（估算，没刻过） | | 同样的做法，不做彩色，也不留彩虹边 | 约 2.35 GB（估算，没刻过） | | 普通数据盘 | 4.7 GB | 这张盘上，带颜色的小格和外圈的彩虹边不存数据，所以比估算的少。 ## 还没做到的 - 只试了一台光驱和一张盘，别的光驱不一定读得出。很想知道其他光驱的结果。 - 这些数据不是普通文件，放进电脑看不到，要用专门的小程序才能读出来。上面那些分开放的做法存的是普通文件，这是它们的优势。 - 如果盘上有一块读不出来，除了多存的那几份原图，那块数据就丢了。目前没有额外的容错，加上的话能存的还会少一些。 - 用这种写法，明暗对比比普通刻图淡。之前的圆环测试盘上，亮暗差距约为普通写法的三分之二（[#150 的扫描](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/150)）。这只是局部一段角度的测量，这张玫瑰盘还没有单独比较过。 - 只用明暗、不做彩色的整张图还没刻过，好不好看还不知道。 - 我们的程序还没发布，想先整理和测试。 更早的讨论：[图像和数据共存 #150](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/150)。
具体实现 程序还没发布，下面是它现在的做法。 1. 测几何。用 disc-probe 的 `geo` 测出这种盘的螺旋参数（`u = 180518.44`，`v = 5.5912`），这样就知道每 16 个字节落在盘面的哪里（沿轨约 34 µm）。 2. 分区。半径 24.6 到 54.4 mm 是图案区，54.4 到 56.0 mm 是 `5F` 环，56.0 到 57.6 mm 是 `A5` 环。外圈从 LBA 约 1,945,558 开始，所以外圈不带数据。 3. 切格。图案区按极坐标切成小格：径向 0.06 mm，角度 0.172°（沿轨约 0.074 到 0.163 mm），共 496 × 2093 格。 4. 决定每格写什么。能显色的区域，用原图的红、蓝通道做误差扩散，每格是红光纹理、蓝光纹理或暗写法。显不出色的上下两块，用亮度做误差扩散，每格是亮写法或暗写法。结果存成 0.02 mm 网格的标签图。 5. 选字节。暗写法 16 种：`62 63 65 67 70 74 75 9C A2 A8 B1 B4 B6 E1 E7 EE`。亮写法 16 种：`5C 7A 7C 86 88 8A 8B 8D 93 95 96 97 9A D2 D5 D7`。按 EFMPlus 码字的跳变数挑选，暗的每 16 位平均 4.55 次跳变，亮的 2.73 次。两组不相交，也和彩色纹理、彩虹边的字节分得开。 6. 打包数据。每个 ECC 块（16 个扇区）是一帧：`RSD1` 魔数、8 字节流偏移、2 字节长度、4 字节 CRC32，共 18 字节头，后面是这段数据。数据流前面放原图，256 MiB 和 512 MiB 处再各放一份，其余是可复现的测试数据。 7. 写入字节。整帧拆成 4 bit 一组，和一段按 LBA 生成的伪随机数异或（否则重复的内容会写出有规律的纹路，影响画面），再查表变成暗或亮的字节。这些是扰码之后想要的字节，所以再异或一次扰码序列，得到写进 ISO 的用户字节。文件系统占前面的扇区，数据从 LBA 32 开始。 8. 刻录。普通 ISO，用 Windows 自带的刻录工具。光驱自己加扇区头和 PI、PO 校验，这些字节我们选不了。 9. 读取。普通读取后异或扰码序列，按 16 字节分组。一组全部属于暗集合或亮集合，就是数据。还原 4 bit，异或同样的伪随机数，校验 CRC。解码不需要设计图，丢一块也只损失那一块。 这张盘的字节占比：暗写法 47.5%，亮写法 11.4%，彩色纹理 25.8%，`5F` 6.4%，`A5` 8.9%。
技术细节 - 读取：LG GH70N，RITEKF1 DVD-R，143,444 个 ECC 块，读取错误 0，121,439 帧共 1,381,080,394 字节逐帧一致，3 份原图 SHA-256 一致。普通读取，非 FUA。 - 编码：在扰码后的字节上，从 16 种短游程字节（暗）或 16 种长游程字节（亮）中选，每字节 4 位。两组字节不相交，解码不需要设计图。 - 每个 ECC 块一帧：魔数、流偏移、长度、CRC32，数据按 LBA 白化。 - 编码器模型抽查 240 块：F512 中位 0%，最高 0.73%（在 `A5` 外圈），没有超过 2% 的块。这是模型值，不是实测的读取余量。 - 约 1.97、2.35 GB 按面积和每字节 4 位算出。 - 对比度依据：#150 里 `mix1` 盘的扫描，`SHORT`/`LONG` 约 0.75 到 0.86，`A5`/`92` 约 0.67 到 0.77。
Implementation (English) The program isn't published yet. This is what it does now. 1. Geometry. disc-probe's `geo` gives the spiral of this disc type (`u = 180518.44`, `v = 5.5912`), so we know where each 16 bytes land on the disc (about 34 µm along the track). 2. Areas. Radius 24.6 to 54.4 mm is the picture, 54.4 to 56.0 mm a `5F` ring, 56.0 to 57.6 mm an `A5` ring. The rings start at about LBA 1,945,558 and hold no data. 3. Cells. The picture is cut into polar cells: 0.06 mm radially and 0.172° around (about 0.074 to 0.163 mm along the track), 496 × 2093 cells. 4. Choosing each cell. Where colour is possible, error diffusion on the original's red and blue channels makes each cell a red-line texture, a blue-line texture or dark. In the top and bottom areas, error diffusion on brightness makes each cell light or dark. The result is a label map on a 0.02 mm grid. 5. Bytes. Dark: `62 63 65 67 70 74 75 9C A2 A8 B1 B4 B6 E1 E7 EE`. Light: `5C 7A 7C 86 88 8A 8B 8D 93 95 96 97 9A D2 D5 D7`. They're picked by transitions in their EFMPlus code words: on average 4.55 per 16 bits for dark and 2.73 for light. The sets don't overlap each other, and they can be told apart from the texture and ring bytes. 6. Framing. Each ECC block (16 sectors) is one frame: an `RSD1` magic, 8-byte stream offset, 2-byte length and 4-byte CRC32, 18 bytes in all, then the data. The stream starts with the original picture, with more copies at 256 MiB and 512 MiB. The rest is reproducible test data. 7. Writing. The frame is split into 4-bit pieces, XORed with a pseudo-random sequence keyed by LBA (otherwise repeating content would write a regular pattern and affect the picture), then mapped to dark or light bytes. Those are the bytes we want after scrambling, so XORing with the scrambler sequence gives the user bytes in the ISO. The file system takes the first sectors, and data starts at LBA 32. 8. Burning. It's a normal ISO, burned with the tool built into Windows. The drive adds its own sector headers and PI and PO parity, which we can't choose. 9. Reading. After a normal read, XOR with the scrambler sequence and split into 16-byte groups. A group whose bytes are all in the dark set or all in the light set is data. Recover the 4-bit pieces, XOR the same pseudo-random sequence and check the CRC. Decoding doesn't need the design, and a lost block only loses itself. Share of bytes on this disc: dark 47.5%, light 11.4%, coloured textures 25.8%, `5F` 6.4%, `A5` 8.9%.
English To get both a picture and files on one disc, the approaches we've seen give the files their own place: the inner or outer ring, the blank parts of the picture ([#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96)), or the other layer of a dual-layer disc ([#59](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/59)). The area with the picture just shows the picture. This disc doesn't keep them apart. About 70% of the picture area is both picture and data: 1.38 GB, about 30% of a normal DVD. The whole disc read back with no errors, and all the data came back exactly as written. The disc also stores 3 copies of the original picture, and all 3 came back intact. This is an early result from one disc and one drive. The limits are listed below. The images above are a photo, the design we burned, and a map of where the data is. The green areas store data: the dark parts of the roses, plus the top and bottom areas that only show light and dark. The coloured cells and the rainbow edge don't. About 70% of the picture area holds data. The colours in the photo are a separate experiment: [#168](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/168). **How the picture and data fit together.** Think of choosing between synonyms when you write a sentence. The meaning stays the same, but which word you chose can itself be a code. On a disc, there are many ways to write a spot that look about equally dark. We picked 16 ways for dark and 16 for light. Choosing one of 16 hides 4 bits in each byte. So the light and dark stay about the same, and the data is in which one we chose. To read it, the drive reads the disc as usual, then a small program turns those choices back into the original data. **How much it holds.** | | | |---|---| | This disc | 1.38 GB, measured | | Same method, no colour, rainbow edge kept | about 1.97 GB (estimate, not burned) | | Same method, no colour, no rainbow edge | about 2.35 GB (estimate, not burned) | | Normal data disc | 4.7 GB | On this disc the coloured cells and the rainbow edge store no data, which is why it holds less than the estimates. **What it can't do yet.** - We've tried one drive and one disc. Other drives may not read it, and we'd love to hear how others do. - The data isn't a normal file. You can't see it on a computer without a small program of ours. The approaches above store normal files, which is their advantage. - If part of the disc can't be read, that data is lost, apart from the extra copies of the picture. There's no extra protection yet, and adding it would reduce the room further. - This way of writing gives less contrast than a normal picture burn. On our earlier ring test disc the gap between light and dark was about two thirds of the normal one ([scan in #150](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/150)). That was measured over a small range of angles, and we haven't compared it on this rose disc. - We haven't burned a whole picture using only light and dark, so we don't know how good it looks. - Our program isn't published yet. We'd like to clean it up and test it first. Earlier discussion: [picture and data #150](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/150). The numbers are in the technical details above.

nodes.body:
我想以此总结下，是不是这样，想出这几种同时有图案与数据的方法，有不对请纠正：

1. 沿径向的一些圈存数据，一些圈来绘图。例如我早期发的 https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/102 就是内圈纯存数据，外圈来画图。这样的话，内圈的数据就是在光盘用户编程区的开头，可以直接放可挂载的光盘fs。就是一张普通的光盘，只不过外圈用不到的地方可以来画图案。同理，当然也可以内圈画一些图案，外圈开始放数据。但这样需要读数据时就要对光盘seek。甚至我想应该还可以利用光盘的session（或CD叫track）来分隔。比如有一些session存图案，一些session放数据。只要相对位置对对好就行了（看cdrskin -minfo中的session next start位置，从DIS图案ISO中相应位置去取就行了）。
2. DIS图案空白处。它不是接收png吗，png中的纯透明部分是会被标记为Unconstrained，就是不刻意控制扰码后结果，让结果随机化。这一部分来存数据。但这样取数据和还原时，应该就得要更多的处理，而且是不是需要知道一些原始图案的信息？
3. DIS图案处，隐写数据。黑/白图案可以对应着不止唯一的Q，那就可以选用不同的扰码Q以此来做隐写。这种方式我觉得存的数据量相对少很多。

@bczhc 总结得很清楚，这三种就是我们知道的做法，也谢谢你补上 #102 和 session 的思路。第 2、3 条我补充几点：

**第 2 种（图案空白处）：** [#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96) 就是这种做法。它把文件放进图案的空白区，按整扇区放，并且在算校验之前就把文件内容固定好。按它的描述，存进去的还是文件夹里的普通文件，读的时候应该不需要原图。这个 PR 我没有实测过，以它的说明为准。

**第 3 种（图案处隐写）：** #170 就是这一种，有两点和你说的不太一样：

- 数据量没有那么少。这张盘实测 1.38 GB，因为每个字节能藏 4 bit，而不是偶尔藏一点。如果不做彩色，只用明暗，估算约 2 到 2.35 GB，这个还没刻过。代价是它不是普通文件，放进电脑看不到，要用小程序才能读，明暗对比也会变淡一些。
- 读取时不需要原图。暗和亮用的是两组不重叠的字节，程序看字节本身就知道这里是数据，以及代表什么。

所以三种可以这样比：

| | 数据是普通文件 | 图案能占满 | 大致容量 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. 分圈或分 session | 是 | 否，要分地方 | 取决于数据占多少圈 |
| 2. 图案空白处 | 是（按 #96 的描述） | 否，取决于图有多少空白 | 取决于空白多少 |
| 3. 图案处隐写 | 否 | 是 | 这张盘 1.38 GB |

第 3 种目前只在一台光驱、一张盘上读过。你之前读桥接盘的那台 ASUS 如果方便，等我们把工具整理好，想请你也试试。

意思第三种的话，用户图案ISO中每一字节能藏一半数据？那藏得挺多。

第二种，它应该是交错的。读出来像是：

DDDDDDDDDDAAAAAAAAAAAAAADDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDAAAAAAAAAAAADDDDDDDDDDD 这种之类的（D是要存的数据，A是艺术图案）。怎么去交错就是问题。仅从镜像里看，似乎不能够分辨哪些是用于艺术图的字节，哪些是实际有意义数据的字节？那pr我还没看。不知道这个实现起难度怎样。

@bczhc 对，第三种里每个带数据的字节藏 4 bit，就是一半。不过这张盘上并不是每个字节都带：彩色小格和外圈不存，所以实际是 1.38 GB，约占整盘三成。如果不做彩色，上限才接近一半。

第二种我看了 [#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96) 的说明和代码片段，它是这样去交错的：把文件切成很多段，放进空白扇区，再用 ISO 9660 的多段（multi-extent）记录写进目录。所以不用从镜像里分辨哪些是图案、哪些是数据，文件系统会记下每一段的位置。按 PR 的说法，一个 12.5 MB 的文件夹被分成了 1,473 段，把各段拼起来和原文件逐字节相同。

有两点要留意：

- 只有整个扇区都落在空白处才能放文件，所以它要求图案有足够的空白。
- PR 验证的是把各段拼起来，我没有看到它写在各个系统上直接挂载的结果，我们自己也没试过。段数这么多时，各系统的兼容性如何，我不清楚。
可能睡8小时离开一会（）谢谢你一直和我讨论这些 ^w^

有关 https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/170#discussioncomment-19433170 中的2，在把unconstrained部分存其他数据，但同时图片透明底上是有图案的，dvd从内向外一圈一圈读，就是交错的数据。要恢复这些数据我觉得是一定要知道一些东西的，比如制作dis iso使用的原图，轨道参数这些，才能知道哪些地方是图案哪些是unconstrained数据才能抽出来还原数据。

但其实今天我又想到了一个更加直接简单的方法。dis iso中按说Q域中只有0x92跟0xa5，剩下的就是一些随机数据（对应图片透明底）。当然采取 https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/90 的一个workaround后，还会出现0x9b这个值。所以，只要把要存的数据中的0x9b 0x92 0xa5这三个字节通过转义全消掉不要出现，再直接填充dis iso中不是0x9b 0x92 0xa5这三个字节的空间（基本上就是透明区域，虽然dis填充的随机数据中也会出现0x9b 0x92 0xa5什么的但非常非常少量）。

解码就是把光盘数据读一遍，读出的内容中的0x9b 0x92 0xa5全删去，剩下的数据就是转义后的用户存的数据，去转义就能恢复到原数据。

代码已经实现在，https://github.com/bczhc/dvd-tools/blob/7f4d7aa0307bae11cf5050ee90a80696d80d4136/src/bin/dvd-hide.rs#L4-L6 且我已经在DVD+RW上测试了一遍，在艺术ISO里嵌入了一个1G多的文件，然后烧录再读取再提取，两者是一样的。

转义表所用的是：

```
A5: 5C 00
92: 5C 01
9B: 5C 02
5C: 5C 5C （转义前缀它自己）
```

@bczhc 这个方法很漂亮！不需要原图和轨道参数，读出来删掉这三种字节就行，转义的开销也很小：随机数据里 4 种字节各约 1/256，平均只多约 1.6%。而且你已经实刻读回一致了，这比我们的还完整。我还没读你的代码，下面只是从描述想到的一点。

有一个地方可能要留意：出现读取错误的时候。这种编码没有“位置”，内容是一串连续的字节，如果某一块读不出来，或者错误恰好落在一个 `5C` 上，后面的转义就可能错位，文件位置也都跟着移了。DVD 上这种盘本身就比普通盘更容易出读取错误，所以这个情况不算罕见。

一个可能的补法：每个 ECC 块（或每 N 字节）单独成帧，带偏移和 CRC，就像我们玫瑰盘那样，一块丢了只损失它自己的内容，帧边界也能重新对齐。如果你已经处理了，就当我没说（）

顺带说一下和隐写的区别：你这种放在透明底，图案部分对比度完全不受影响；隐写能用满整张图，但对比度有代价。所以图有大片透明底时，你这个更合适。
当然这个dvd-hide程序所输入的ISO一定要是通过#90 中的脚本（或dvd-tools项目中也有dsv-balancer就是做这个的）处理过一遍的，不然dvd会读不出

> 就当我没说（）

怎么这AI也发（）了 XD

对了，然后我这套方法呢，输入的要放的数据是会经过一次aes-256-ctr加密的，说是加密但iv跟密钥都是填零的，它的作用我只是当scramble。因为这个数据是在Q域进行转义后直接填充的，如果这个文件里有很多重复杀手字节什么之类的就又会影响DVD读盘了。所以直接给它做个扰码，给它随机化。就像DVD本身自己会做的一样、、

title: Auto-calibration for bluray (BD-R and BD-RE) discs
body: @Ashley-QwQ demonstrated how to calibrate wasting only one DVD-R disc on a drive that supports CAV (constant angular velocity): https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/108#discussioncomment-19403199. I did a quick Google search and it seems that some Bluray drives also support CAV mode for reading. That means that the same one-disc calibration may be possible for BD-R. Maybe I am wrong and some software or hardware limitations prevent this calibration method from working properly.

nodes.body:
@LTVA1 Thanks for bringing this up. I think the idea can work, though nobody has tried it yet, and as you guessed, the open question is the drive.

The geometry carries over. DIS models a BD-R as the same kind of spiral as a DVD, and a Blu-ray read block (71.7 mm of track) is close to a DVD one (82.5 mm), so a timed read should locate an angle about as finely. A BD-R has about 106,000 turns against about 46,000 on a DVD, so the fit has to be tighter, but the method gets there in steps anyway.

Three things are missing:

- A drive that behaves. The only Blu-ray timing we have is bczhc's ASUS BW-16D1H-U: about 9705 rpm on the inner and middle disc, about 1655 rpm at the outer edge, about 200 µs of noise, and speed requests ignored. Its DVD results weren't good enough to burn with either. The method needs one steady speed and low noise.
- A measuring disc burned without a spare area. According to the DIS docs, the usual Windows burning interface can assume a spare area, while DIS writes without one. A disc burned the usual way may not match a DIS burn, and our burn script uses that same interface, so it wouldn't do here.
- Code. `geo` only has DVD and CD settings so far, and the preset export is the same.

On BD-RE: the DIS docs list only single-layer BD-R, so a BD-RE measurement would have no burn route yet.

The cost also differs a little from DVD. You'd still use one measuring disc and then burn pictures, but that disc would be a full 25 GB, about 23 minutes at 4x.

The first step needs no new code, if you or anyone reading has a Blu-ray drive and a BD-R already burned with plain data:

```
python -m discprobe timing --drive X:
```

It only reads, and it prints the speed and the noise. On DVD, the drives that gave good results had roughly under 1° of jitter. If a drive looks steady on Blu-ray, adding BD to `geo` would be worth doing, and existing presets such as Verbatim 64293 would give us something to compare against before burning a picture.

A short update from #107: two Blu-ray drives have now been timed, and neither gave a usable CAV.

- MATSHITA UJ272 (domerawind): constant linear velocity on BD-R, about 1.6x by default or when asked for 3324 kB/s, and about 2.1x when asked for 8990 or 26974 kB/s. A disc with plain data also ran about 2.1x with the CAV bit set, so the bit changed nothing. Its `info` does report 26974 kB/s as CAV, but the reads didn't follow that.
- ASUS BW-16D1H-U (bczhc): constant linear velocity at about 2x when asked for 5540 kB/s. Earlier, with no speed request, it ran about 9705 rpm on the inner and middle disc and about 1655 rpm at the outer edge, with about 200 µs of noise, which is about 12° at that speed.

With constant linear velocity, the spindle speed keeps changing with radius, so read times can't be turned into disc angles. So the method doesn't work on these two drives, and for now adding Blu-ray to `geo` wouldn't have a drive to run on.

That says nothing yet about other models. If anyone has a different Blu-ray drive, one `timing` run on a burned BD-R will show its rotation mode, and a drive that holds one steady speed across the disc would reopen this.

I have ordered LG WH16NS40, it seems to support the CAV at 8x or 12x speed for BD-R. It will arrive in a few weeks (shopping app says November 18th to November 29th). I will test it when it arrives. It's the cheapest drive supporting multilayer bluray and cav for bluray I could find. Will there be any problem with testing it on BD-RE instead of BD-R? I have ordered one BD-RE disc for tests so I can do many measurement and calibration passes.

@LTVA1 Thank you, a drive that may hold CAV is exactly what's missing here, and I hope it turns up early.

BD-RE is fine for the first question, which is whether the drive holds one steady speed and how noisy it is. `timing` only reads, and you can run it on the BD-RE as many times as you like. A few things could trip you up:

- Fill most of the disc first. `timing` looks near the inner, middle and outer parts of the recorded area, and I don't know what a drive does when asked to read formatted but unwritten BD-RE sectors. `python -m discprobe random --sectors N --output iso/bd-random.iso` makes the image. Take N from `info` and leave some margin below it, since an image that exactly fills a disc has been refused by burning software before. A full write at BD-RE's 2x takes about 45 minutes.
- Use kB/s for the speed. `--speed 8x` uses the DVD 1x, so it would ask for the wrong rate. 8x is `--speed 35960` and 12x is `--speed 53940`. For example: `python -m discprobe timing --drive X: --speed 35960`.
- A drive can treat BD-RE and BD-R differently, so CAV on one doesn't promise CAV on the other. It's worth running `timing` on a burned BD-R as well if you get one.
- Watch the noise. The nominal speed at the outer edge is about 6480 rpm at 8x and about 9710 rpm at 12x, so even 50 µs of noise is about 2° at 8x and about 3° at 12x. On DVD, the drives that gave good results stayed roughly under 1°. If the drive offers a slower CAV speed, that may suit this better.

A BD-RE result also wouldn't carry over to BD-R. Disc geometry varies between disc types and batches, and as far as I know a formatted BD-RE has a spare area that shifts sector positions. DIS only burns single-layer BD-R for now, so a BD-RE can test the drive and the method, but it can't produce a preset for your pictures.

You may not need the rewrites for measuring. Measuring never writes, so one burned BD-R can be measured over and over, the same as a BD-RE. A rewritable disc would only save you discs on burn tests, and DIS doesn't burn BD-RE yet.

No hurry at all. If `timing` shows steady CAV with low noise, please post the output here and adding Blu-ray to `geo` becomes worth doing.

title: 刻录同时具有音频轨道和图案的Audio CD
body: DiscImageStudio 项目在 CD 模式下具有随盘文件功能，但加载文件之后会将 CD 作为数据光盘处理。 而若想使 CD 放入旧型号随身听等没那么智能的播放器播放（不支持 MP3 CD 这样的 Data CD 模式，只按照最老的红皮书 CD-DA 格式解码 PCM 流的旧型号），就需要产生符合 CD-DA 标准的音频盘。 发帖时的 Release 是1.4.2，这个版本可以产生占满 CD 全长的 CD-DA 模式音频文件，但不支持从开头截断一定长度用来预留音轨区，也不支持导入CUE。 笔者尝试手动截断开头并与音轨拼接，获得了成功，得到了内圈是音轨，外圈是图案的CD-DA音频模式CD，于是分享经验，并抛砖引玉探讨能否作为一项功能引入DiscImageStudio。 测试使用三菱 CD-RW 光盘，已完成校准，此光盘共有336075扇区，时长74:41.00，扇区数和时长吻合（(74*60+41)*75=336075），数据如下 ` "geometry": { "innerRadiusMm": 24.880391237427595, "outerRadiusMm": 57.79370167081931, "sectors": 336075, "pitchLinear": -4.9058082387912915E-05, "pitchQuadratic": 6.285612004335759E-05, "pitchCubic": -3.07381200748645E-05 }, ` 完成图案部分设计后在 DiscImageStudio 中导出 wav 文件，同时得到.cue文件，但此时的cue文件只记录了一条占满CD全长的音轨 下一步是准备要刻录的音频轨道并计算时间长度，这里时长的格式是分:秒.帧 帧是CD-DA里最小的一个时长单位，一秒由75帧组成，一帧内的单个通道有588个采样点组成，这里为了规避帧长度未对齐可能带来的影响，我在导出音频工程时提前将其裁剪为了整数。 接下来我使用 Exact Audio Copy 软件来编辑 CUE 文件 首先导入要刻录的两端音轨，之后计算音轨占用的时长（包含可能需要的静音段），结果为07:45.00 接下来是从 DiscImageStudio 中导出的图案 wav 文件中从前段减去这段时长，那么处理前的wav文件长度为74:41.00，处理后的wav文件长度变为66:56.00 将这段音频附加在音频轨道后，得到这样的布局和CUE文件 刻录这个文件就能得到内圈为音频，外圈为图案的CD-DA光盘，经测试，可以在CD播放器（应该是仅能解码PCM流的老方案）上读出音频，美中不足的是播放器也能识别到作为图案的第三轨，播放到时会发出噪音xD

title: [Experiment] Storing data in a DVD's picture area: an idea and an early test / 【实验】让 DVD 的图案区域同时存数据：一个想法和初步测试
body:
[中文版点这里](#zh) With DiscImageStudio, files and a picture currently occupy separate parts of a disc. The files go in an inner or outer ring, or in the picture's blank areas, as in [#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96). We want to try storing data in the area that draws the picture, too. If several different bytes can produce the same brightness, then choosing among them could carry data. But picture discs often fail to read back at all ([#90](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/90)), so the first step is to make that area readable. | Question | What we know so far | |---|---| | Can a small change make an unreadable block readable? | Yes in one test, limited to one drive, one disc and one block; a second drive and disc also point to the same cause | | Can a whole picture disc be read back? | Yes on one drive and disc: bczhc read a whole changed disc with no errors. 301 sampled blocks also read on our GH70N | | Does the change affect the picture? | No clear change near the centre of the scanner's dark region, and a possible small loss toward its edges. One pair of discs and one scanner | | Can the picture area also store data? | Not shown yet. Rings of two random-byte mixes read on one drive and differ in brightness on one scanner | This is still an experiment, and I'll update this post as we get results. ## How a picture gets onto a disc DIS draws light and dark areas with different bytes. On our discs, areas filled with the byte `92` look bright, and areas filled with `A5` look dark. Mixing the two makes grey. A disc records data as pits and lands along a spiral, and the length of a continuous pit or land is called a run. Each byte turns into roughly one pattern of runs, which also depends on the byte before it: `92` gives long runs and `A5` gives short ones. The drive scrambles data before encoding it, so DIS undoes that step in advance. After the drive scrambles the data, its encoder sees exactly the `92` or `A5` the picture needs. ## How the picture could also store data A small patch of picture that looks evenly bright covers a lot of bytes. A 0.2 mm square is about 270 tracks of about 94 bytes each, so roughly 25,000 bytes on the disc, all currently used to produce one brightness. About 21,000 of those are ours to choose; the rest are parity and sync that the drive adds. If other long-run bytes also look bright, we could choose among them, and that choice would represent data. Dark areas would choose among short-run bytes in the same way. To get the data back, you'd read the disc normally and turn each byte back into bits with a small decoder. An ordinary file put straight on the disc wouldn't do this: whatever the file contains, the drive's scrambling turns it into something close to random, so it shows up grey. Whether this works depends on one thing we haven't measured: whether a mix of long-run bytes really looks bright and a mix of short-run bytes really looks dark. Contrast will drop, and colour may fade too. Capacity depends on the same thing, and we don't have a real number yet. As one cautious estimate, if only stretches of plain `92` and `A5` look right, and each stretch must be 32 bytes long, a mid-grey disc holds at most about 18 MB. This is a calculation, not a measurement.
Details: the steps, and the numbers from our model The steps would be: 1. Sort bytes into a long-run set and a short-run set. DIS's `dispersion-byte-pools.json` already has this kind of grouping. 2. For each bright byte in the picture, use the data to choose from the long-run set. For a dark byte, choose from the short-run set. Grey is a mix. 3. Undo the scrambling and burn. The drive adds its usual header and parity, so reading uses its normal error correction. 4. To read, recover the bytes by redoing the scrambling, then turn them back into bits. The data needs its own error correction on top, in case a sector is lost. Numbers from our encoder model, for one block with full frames. DSV is explained in the next section. Whether brightness follows the mean run is still an assumption. | What's written | Mean run | Data per byte | Peak DSV | |---|---|---|---| | All `92` | 7.28T | 0 | 315 | | 32 long-run bytes at random | 5.50T | 5 bits | 62 | | Random data | 4.72T | about 8 bits | 25 | | 19 short-run bytes at random | 3.85T | 4.2 bits | 37 | | All `A5` | 3.39T | 0 | 325 | One T is one channel bit, about 133 nm. Each byte becomes a 16-bit EFMPlus code word. If single bytes from these sets work, at 5 and 4.2 bits per byte, the ideal limit on a 4.7 GB disc is about 2.5 to 2.9 GB. That assumes single-byte mixes show light and dark, which is untested, and it's before the data's own error correction, guard bytes and any layout overhead. The drive's parity isn't in this figure, since 4.7 GB is already what's left after it.
## Why we started with reading, and what we tested bczhc found a block from a DIS picture ISO that the drive can't read at blocks 2000, 4000 and 8000 (it reports an uncorrectable read error, `3/11/05`), but that reads fine elsewhere. Scrambling depends on the sector's position, so the same data only turns back into `92` and `A5` at some positions, and those are the ones that fail. Our model shows the same split: a large imbalance between pits and lands at those positions, and a small one elsewhere. That imbalance is called DSV. The encoder normally keeps it near zero, and we suspect a large DSV upsets the read signal. Our best explanation is that `92` has two possible code words. One is balanced. The other pushes DSV the same way on every byte. Normally the encoder steers DSV by choosing between alternative code words, but in the middle of a run of `92` it has no alternative to choose, so it can't switch back until the next sync code. Which form you get depends on the byte before the run. That part follows from the standard's code tables; that this is what makes the read fail is still our suspicion. So we changed the first `92` of each run to `9B`, a byte that forces the balanced form. That's 168 bytes out of 32768. On one disc and one drive, bczhc then got this: | Block | Data | Read | |---|---|---| | 2000, 8000 | original | fails | | 4000 | original (bczhc's earlier run) | fails | | 4000 | with `9B` | reads | | 3999 | original, but at this position it doesn't turn into `92` and `A5` | reads | The change didn't make reading slower through retries: block 4000 took 76.2 ms and block 3999, which has no such problem, took 76.9 ms. Thanks to bczhc for the test. An AI review found a bug in our encoder and proposed `75` and `9B`, and we recalculated its numbers with our own code. This doesn't show that DSV is the cause on other drives. Update: we then tested the cause directly. On a burned comparison disc and a GH70N, a drive that rarely reports errors, we read 9 blocks of each texture. `92D` is plain `92` with one extra byte at the start of each frame, which pushes it into the unbalanced form. | Written | Reads | Fails | |---|---|---| | `92D` | 0 | 9, about 9 to 11 s each | | `92` | 8 | 1, and some reads take about 10 s | | `A5`, 92/A5 mixes, long-run and short-run mixes, random data | 9 of 9 each | 0 | This is one disc and one drive, but it is the first time we changed only the form of `92` and saw reading change. Peak DSV alone doesn't predict it: `A5` peaks at 325 in the model and reads fine, because that peak is only in its parity rows, while `92D` peaks at 373 and is offset in every frame. How long the offset lasts may matter more than how high it gets. Second update: whole-disc and scan results. bczhc ran `bridge_iso.py` ([ef38742](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/commit/ef38742)) on a whole picture ISO and burned it on the same Verbatim DVD+RW, read on the same ASUS BW-16D1H-U. The script changed 1.91% of the bytes. `pv` then read all 4.38 GiB without an error. An earlier version of the script had only moved the first error from about 390 MiB to about 2.14 GiB. By eye, bczhc sees no real change in the picture. We burned one picture with and without the change on RITEKF1. On the GH70N, 301 sampled blocks of the changed disc all read and matched, with 4 slow reads of 2 to 9 s. We then scanned the two discs together 3 times: ![Original and bridged discs, with picture contrast for each scan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/dense-bridged/compare.png?v=2) Notes on this figure: - The numbers in this figure compare the picture's light parts with the background, as a difference in log brightness. They come from small patches within 9° of the centre of the scanner's dark region. Both discs average about 0.19, a brightness difference of about 21%. Each value is uncertain by about 0.02, so a change smaller than about 2 to 3 percentage points wouldn't show. - The strips don't line up with each other because the two burns start at angles about 16° apart. Each one sits next to the design at its own angle. - The white marks are scratches and dust, not picture. They were clipped before measuring. - This is one pair of discs on one scanner, and only in that narrow region. We didn't measure other viewing angles or a camera. A closer look changes this a little. The numbers above only cover the centre of the dark region, and contrast depends strongly on the angle from that centre. Here it is split by angle, averaged over the 3 scans: | Angle from the centre of the dark region | Original | Bridged | |---|---|---| | -14° to -10° | 0.083 | 0.049 | | -10° to -6° | 0.097 | 0.093 | | -6° to -2° | 0.215 | 0.210 | | -2° to 2° | 0.261 | 0.210 | | 2° to 6° | 0.204 | 0.208 | | 6° to 10° | 0.149 | 0.140 | | 10° to 14° | 0.084 | 0.064 | Most of the central bins are close. From -2° to 2° the original is higher, but that comes mainly from one high value (0.332 in scan 3), and values in that bin are uncertain by 0.02 to 0.07. From 10° to 14° out, on both sides, the bridged disc is lower in all 3 scans. That could be real, since changing the code word of `92` can change where the light goes. But the signal there is faint, it rests on few patches, the 3 scans are of the same two discs, and the discs show different parts of the picture at those angles. So the result so far is no clear change near the centre of the dark region, and a possible small loss toward its edges. A fixed camera at other angles should help settle it. Here is the same part of the picture on both discs: ![The same part of the picture on the original and bridged discs, with their difference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/dense-bridged/aligned.png) In the Difference column, figures look dark on the left and light on the right. That mostly comes from position: at the left of each strip the original is near the centre of the dark region and the bridged disc near its edge, and at the right it's the reverse. So this figure shows the two pictures line up, but it can't be used on its own to measure a loss. The comparison disc shows something for the data idea too. In the same dark region, the two random-byte mixes differ in brightness: ![Ring brightness on the comparison disc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/mix1/scan_rings.png) Notes on this figure: - Each ring is compared with the random-data ring in its own group. Single rings are noisy, because that reference ring is noisy and the outer rings have a smudge. - Comparing pairs in the same group is steadier. `SHORT` over `LONG` is 0.75 to 0.86 in all 6 pairs, while `A5` over `92` is 0.67 to 0.77. So on this measure, the gap between these two random mixes is about two thirds of the gap between the two solid bytes. - About 15° away from the centre of the dark region the differences mostly fade, to within about 6% of random data. - These are plain rings of random bytes. We haven't drawn a picture with them or stored and recovered a file. Third update: how much bias does it take? A new test disc (`tools/duty_disc.py`) held 92 with biased bursts. The bursts stayed the same, so peak DSV stayed at about 269, and only their spacing changed. On a GH70N with RITEKF1, each condition got 60 reads: ![Reads that failed against the share of time at high bias](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/duty1/result.png) | Burst spacing (data frames) | Share of time at high bias | Reads that failed | |---|---:|---:| | 96 | 0.85% | 3 | | 64 | 1.2% | 0 | | 32 | 2.4% | 10 | | 16 | 4.6% | 41 | | 8 | 9.4% | 59 | | 4 | 17% | 57 | | 2 | 34% | 60 | | 1 | 66% | 60 | "Share of time at high bias" is the share of 512T windows whose mean level is above 0.125 in the model (F512). Every block that did read matched the ISO. So on this drive, trouble starts somewhere between about 2% and 5%. Plain `92` (2.8%) failed 12 of 60, close to the 2.4% row, and plain `A5` (0.7%), whose peak is over 300, failed none. This fits the earlier result that peak DSV alone doesn't predict reading. It also explains why the guard byte helps: it brings this share close to 0. Burst length matters too. With the same number of biased bytes per block, 8-byte bursts failed 5 of 60, 16-byte 24, 32-byte 26 and 64-byte 59. Some of this isn't explained. 8-byte bursts failed 5 times at a share of only 0.2%. 32-byte bursts failed in whole segments, with some segments all failing and others all reading, and the share doesn't predict which. And this is one disc and one drive: bczhc's ASUS fails on blocks at about 2.7% to 4%, while the GH70N still reads most blocks there. The limit depends on the drive, so these numbers aren't a rule for other drives. [Every read is recorded here](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/main/evidence/duty1/readback.json). An AI review proposed this metric and test, and we recalculated its numbers with our own code.
Details: the code words, and the DSV numbers `92` has two EFMPlus code words: - States 1 and 3: `0000100000001000`, runs of 8T and 8T, no offset, next state 3. - States 2 and 4: `0100000000010000`, runs of 6T and 10T, an offset of 4 per byte, next state 2. Only bytes 00 to 57h have a second table of code words for steering DSV, and `92` and `A5` don't. Bytes above that have two forms only in states 1 and 4, so once `92` is in state 2 the encoder has no alternative and can't correct the offset. Over about 79 bytes that adds up to about 316, the calculated size of one jump. `75` and `9B` lead to the first form from every state, which we checked by listing all the cases. Peak DSV in the model: about 310 for bczhc's block where it fails (307 to 311), about 24 where it reads, about 25 to 29 for random data depending on the seed, and 315 for all `92`. The position matters because the scrambler has 16 starting values, so the block only turns back into `92` and `A5` at matching positions.
## What we don't know yet - Whether this holds on other drives and discs. So far a whole disc has been read on one drive. - Whether the parity the drive adds causes trouble elsewhere. `tools/bridge_iso.py` doesn't touch it, and it can still have a large DSV. On a test image some blocks stay at 100 to 175 in the model. - Whether the picture looks the same at other angles and to a camera. - Whether mixes of bytes can draw a usable picture, and how much data they can really hold.
Details: parity and the picture The drive adds a header to each sector and PI and PO parity over each ECC block of 16 sectors. We can't choose those bytes directly. With uniform data, every column gives the same PO byte, so a PO row becomes one long repeat. All `A5` peaks at 325 there, while its data rows stay at 17. For an ideal grating, going from 6T/10T to 8T/8T makes the first order about 17% stronger and removes the even orders. That can't tell us what a real disc will look like.
## What's next - More drives and discs reading a changed picture disc. - A real picture drawn with the long-run and short-run mixes, checked with a camera as well as the scanner. - Fixing parity rows only if a drive turns out to need it. On the GH70N, `A5` peaks high in those rows and still reads. - The same test disc on a stricter drive, to see how much the limit moves. ## How you can help If you have a picture disc that won't read, run this on the same ISO, burn it on the same kind of disc, and post whether it reads and what it looks like. Failing LBAs help, and a photo next to the original helps most. ```bash python tools/bridge_iso.py your.iso your_bridged.iso --check 24 ``` Related work: [#59](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/59) got stable DVD-R DL burns with a low-DSV palette plus 10% random bytes, and the maintainer's note in #90 warns that mixing in other data doesn't always help. Philips US7990837B2 makes visible marks by steering the encoder, which an ordinary burn command can't do. [#27](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/27) suggests a different route, with the picture and the data on separate layers of a dual-layer disc. We haven't tested dual-layer discs. @bczhc I've quoted your results here, so please correct anything I got wrong. --- ## 中文版 目前，用 DiscImageStudio 在一张盘上同时放文件和图案，还是要把两者分开放：文件放在内圈、外圈，或者像 [#96](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/96) 那样，放在图案的空白处。 我们想试试：用来画图的那片区域，能不能也存数据？如果几种不同的字节能产生同样的明暗，在它们之间选择就能表示数据。不过图案盘经常连读取都有问题（[#90](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/90)），所以第一步是让这片区域读得出来。 | 问题 | 目前的结果 | |---|---| | 读不出的块，小改之后能恢复吗？ | 在一次测试中可以；范围仅限一台光驱、一张盘、一个块；另一台光驱和另一张盘的结果也指向同一个原因 | | 整张图案盘能读出来吗？ | 在一台光驱和一张盘上可以：bczhc 读完了改过的整张盘，没有报错。我们的 GH70N 抽查 301 块也都读出了 | | 修改后，图案会变吗？ | 扫描仪暗区中央没有明显变化，往边缘可能有一点损失。只有一对盘、一台扫描仪 | | 图案区域能同时存数据吗？ | 还没有证实。两种随机字节混合的圆环，在一台光驱上能读，在一台扫描仪上亮度不同 | 这还是个实验，有新结果我会继续更新这篇帖子。 ### 图是怎么刻上去的 DIS 用不同的字节来画出明暗。在我们的盘上，重复写入字节 `92` 的区域看起来亮，重复写入 `A5` 的区域看起来暗，灰色由两者混合而成。 光盘沿一条螺旋线，用坑和岸记录数据，连续一段坑或岸的长度叫作“游程”。每个字节大致对应一组游程，具体还取决于前一个字节：`92` 的游程长，`A5` 的游程短。 光驱在编码前会先对数据做“扰码”，所以 DIS 事先抵消这一步，让光驱扰码后，编码器看到的正好是画图需要的 `92` 或 `A5`。 ### 图案怎么同时存数据 图案中一小块看起来明暗一致的区域，其实覆盖了很多字节。一块 0.2 mm 见方的区域约有 270 条轨道，每条约 94 个字节，盘上加起来约 25000 个字节，现在它们都用来表现同一个亮度。其中约 21000 个是我们能选的，其余是光驱加的校验和同步码。 如果其他长游程字节也能显得亮，我们就可以在它们之间选择，用这个选择来表示数据。暗的区域同样在短游程字节之间选择。取数据时，正常读盘，再用一个小解码器把字节变回数据。普通文件直接放进去做不到这一点：不管文件内容是什么，光驱扰码后都接近随机，刻出来就是灰的。 这能不能行，取决于一件我们还没测的事：长游程字节的混合是不是真的显得亮，短游程字节的混合是不是真的显得暗。对比度一定会下降，颜色也可能变淡。 容量也取决于这一点，现在还没有可靠的数字。保守估算：如果只有连续的 `92`、`A5` 才看得对，而且每段要连续 32 个字节，中灰的盘最多约 18 MB。这是计算，不是测量。
细节：具体步骤和模型里的数字 步骤是： 1. 把字节分成长游程组和短游程组。DIS 的 `dispersion-byte-pools.json` 已经有类似的分组。 2. 图案里亮的字节，用数据决定从长游程组选哪个；暗的字节从短游程组选。灰色是两者混合。 3. 抵消扰码后刻录。光驱照常加扇区头和校验，所以读取时用的是它原有的纠错。 4. 读取时，重新扰码还原字节，再变回数据。数据上面还要有自己的纠错，以防丢掉整个扇区。 下面是编码器模型里的数字，按完整录制帧算一个块。DSV 在下一节解释。“明暗跟着平均游程走”目前还只是假设。 | 写入内容 | 平均游程 | 每字节可带 | DSV 峰值 | |---|---|---|---| | 全 `92` | 7.28T | 0 | 315 | | 32 种长游程字节随机选 | 5.50T | 5 bit | 62 | | 随机数据 | 4.72T | 约 8 bit | 25 | | 19 种短游程字节随机选 | 3.85T | 4.2 bit | 37 | | 全 `A5` | 3.39T | 0 | 325 | 1T 是一个通道位，约 133 nm。每个字节会变成一个 16 位的 EFMPlus 码字。 如果这两组字节单个混用也行，按每字节 5 和 4.2 bit 算，4.7 GB 的盘理想上限约 2.5 到 2.9 GB。前提是单字节混合还能显出明暗，这没测过；也还没扣数据自己的纠错、守护字节和布局开销。光驱的校验不用再扣，4.7 GB 已经是扣掉它之后的容量。
### 为什么先研究读取，以及测到了什么 bczhc 发现 DIS 的一个图案 ISO 里有一个块，写到块 2000、4000、8000 光驱读不出（报告无法纠正的读取错误 `3/11/05`），写到别处能读。扰码和扇区位置有关，同样的数据只有写到特定位置才会还原成 `92` 和 `A5`，读不出的正是这些位置。我们的模型里也有同样的差别：这几个位置的坑和岸严重不平衡，别处很小。这种不平衡叫 DSV。编码器平时会让它接近 0，我们怀疑它太大会干扰读取信号。 我们目前最好的解释是，`92` 有两种码字。一种是平衡的。另一种每个字节都把 DSV 往同一边推。编码器平时靠在备选码字之间选择来控制 DSV，但一长串 `92` 中间没有备选可挑，所以到下一个同步码之前都换不回来。走哪一种，取决于这段 `92` 前面的字节。这部分能从标准的码表推出来；读不出是不是因为它，还只是我们的怀疑。 所以我们把每段 `92` 的第一个字节改成 `9B`，它能让后面的 `92` 走平衡的那种。32768 个字节里改了 168 个。同一张盘、同一台光驱，bczhc 的结果是： | 块 | 数据 | 读取 | |---|---|---| | 2000、8000 | 原版 | 读不出 | | 4000 | 原版（bczhc 之前那次） | 读不出 | | 4000 | 改了 `9B` | 能读 | | 3999 | 原版，但这个位置还原不成 `92` 和 `A5` | 能读 | 改动后也没有因为反复重试而变慢：块 4000 读取 76.2 ms，本来就没问题的块 3999 是 76.9 ms。 感谢 bczhc 做了这次测试。AI 在核对时找出了我们编码器的一个 bug，并提出了 `75`、`9B`，相关数字我们已用自己的代码重新计算。这不能说明在别的光驱上也是 DSV 造成的。 更新：我们随后直接测了原因。在一张刻好的对比盘上，用平时很少报错的 GH70N，每种纹理读 9 块。`92D` 就是普通的 `92`，只在每帧开头多一个字节，把它推进不平衡的那种码字。 | 写入内容 | 能读 | 读不出 | |---|---|---| | `92D` | 0 | 9，每块约 9 到 11 秒 | | `92` | 8 | 1，有些读取要约 10 秒 | | `A5`、`92`/`A5` 混合、长短游程混合、随机数据 | 各 9 块全能读 | 0 | 这只是一张盘、一台光驱，但这是第一次只改变 `92` 的码字形式，读取就跟着变。DSV 峰值单独预测不了：`A5` 模型峰值 325，却读得很好，因为峰值只在校验行；`92D` 峰值 373，而且每一帧都偏。偏多久可能比偏多高更重要。 第二次更新：整盘读取和扫描结果。 bczhc 用 `bridge_iso.py`（[ef38742](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/commit/ef38742)）处理了一个完整的图案 ISO，还是刻到同款 Verbatim DVD+RW，用同一台 ASUS BW-16D1H-U 读。脚本改了 1.91% 的字节。之后 `pv` 读完了全部 4.38 GiB，没有报错。旧版脚本只是把第一个错误从约 390 MiB 推到约 2.14 GiB。bczhc 目视，图案看不出什么变化。 我们用 RITEKF1 把同一张图加和不加改动各刻了一张。在 GH70N 上，改过的盘抽查 301 块，全部读出且内容一致，其中 4 块偏慢（2 到 9 秒）。然后把两张盘放在一起扫了 3 次： ![原版和桥接版的对比，以及每次扫描的图案对比度](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/dense-bridged/compare.png?v=2) 这张图的说明（图上的文字是英文，Original 是原版，Bridged 是桥接版）： - 这些只是随机字节组成的圆环，我们还没有用它们画图，也没有存入再取回过文件。 第三次更新：偏多少才读不出？我们做了一张新的测试盘（`tools/duty_disc.py`），在 `92` 里放有偏置的突发。突发本身不变，所以 DSV 峰值都约 269，只改变突发之间的间隔。GH70N 加 RITEKF1，每种读 60 次： ![读不出的比例和高偏置占比的关系](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/main/evidence/duty1/result.png) | 突发间隔（数据帧） | 高偏置占比 | 读不出 | |---|---:|---:| | 96 | 0.85% | 3 | | 64 | 1.2% | 0 | | 32 | 2.4% | 10 | | 16 | 4.6% | 41 | | 8 | 9.4% | 59 | | 4 | 17% | 57 | | 2 | 34% | 60 | | 1 | 66% | 60 | “高偏置占比”是模型里平均电平绝对值超过 0.125 的 512T 窗口所占的比例（F512）。能读出的块，内容都和 ISO 一致。图上的文字是英文。 所以在这台光驱上，问题大约从 2% 到 5% 之间开始。纯 `92`（2.8%）读不出 12 次，和 2.4% 那一行接近；纯 `A5`（0.7%）峰值 300 多，一次都没失败。这和之前“DSV 峰值单独预测不了”的结果对得上，也解释了守护字节为什么有用：它把这个占比压到接近 0。 突发长度也有影响。每块偏置字节数相同时，8 字节的突发读不出 5 次，16 字节 24 次，32 字节 26 次，64 字节 59 次。 有些地方还解释不了。8 字节的突发占比只有 0.2%，也失败了 5 次。32 字节的突发是成段失败的，有的段全失败，有的段全成功，占比预测不了是哪些。而且这只是一张盘、一台光驱：bczhc 的 ASUS 在约 2.7% 到 4% 的块上读不出，GH70N 在这里大多还能读。界限和光驱有关，这些数字不能套用到别的光驱。[每次读取的记录在这里](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/main/evidence/duty1/readback.json)。这个指标和测试是 AI 审查提出的，数字我们已用自己的代码重新计算。
细节：码字和 DSV 的数字 `92` 的两种 EFMPlus 码字： - 状态 1、3：`0000100000001000`，游程 8T 和 8T，没有偏置，下一状态 3。 - 状态 2、4：`0100000000010000`，游程 6T 和 10T，每个字节偏 4，下一状态 2。 只有 00 到 57h 的字节才有第二套码字用来控制 DSV，`92`、`A5` 不在其中。更大的字节只在状态 1、4 下有两种写法，所以 `92` 一旦到了状态 2，编码器就没有别的码字可选，也就无法纠正这段偏移。约 79 个字节累积约 316，这是算出来的一次跳变大小。`75`、`9B` 在所有状态下都通向第一种，我们逐一枚举确认过。 模型里的 DSV 峰值：bczhc 的块在失败位置约 310（307 到 311），能读的位置约 24；随机数据约 25 到 29，随种子变化；全 `92` 是 315。 位置有影响，是因为扰码初值只有 16 种，这个块只有在匹配的位置才会还原成 `92` 和 `A5`。
### 还不知道的 - 换别的光驱和盘是否也成立。目前只在一台光驱上读完过整张盘。 - 光驱加的校验会不会在别处造成问题。`tools/bridge_iso.py` 不处理校验，校验部分的 DSV 仍可能很大。测试镜像里有些块在模型中还剩 100 到 175。 - 换别的角度和相机看，图案是否还一样。 - 字节混合能不能画出可用的图案，实际能存多少数据。
细节：校验和图案 光驱会给每个扇区加扇区头，并给每 16 个扇区（一个 ECC 块）加 PI、PO 校验，这些字节我们不能直接指定。数据均匀时，每列算出的 PO 字节都一样，PO 行就成了一长串重复。全 `A5` 的峰值 325 就在这里，它的数据行只有 17。 按理想光栅计算，从 6T/10T 变成 8T/8T，一级衍射增强约 17%，偶数级消失。不过这还不能告诉我们实际刻出来是什么样。
### 接下来 - 用更多光驱和盘读改过的图案盘。 - 用长、短游程混合真正画一张图，除了扫描仪也用相机看。 - 校验行的问题，等确实有光驱需要时再处理。GH70N 上 `A5` 在这些行的峰值很高，也还能读。 - 用更严格的光驱读同样的测试盘，看界限移动多少。 ### 可以怎么帮忙 如果你有读不出的图案盘，可以用同一个 ISO 跑下面这条，刻到同款盘上，回帖说读不读得出、看起来怎样。出错的 LBA 有用，和原版放一起的照片最有用。 ```bash python tools/bridge_iso.py your.iso your_bridged.iso --check 24 ``` 相关的工作：[#59](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/pull/59) 用低 DSV 调色板加 10% 随机字节，让 DVD-R DL 刻录稳定了；维护者在 #90 提醒过，混入别的数据不一定都有改善。Philips US7990837B2 通过控制编码器做出可见标记，普通刻录命令做不到。[#27](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/27) 提了另一条路：在双层盘上把图案和数据分层存放。双层盘我们还没有测过。 @bczhc 这里引用了你的结果，有写错的地方麻烦指正。

nodes.body: 说起来，目前的DVD的深浅色，我感觉可能是由于光栅常数的不同，深色是把可见光的一级衍射角度挪到了非常偏的角度上实现的，所以似乎应该只会和游程有关系。

@NaiveTomcat 这个想法我们也觉得很可能。按光栅方程算，`92` 的主周期约 2.13 µm，550 nm 的绿光一级偏约 15°；`A5` 约 0.85 µm，要偏约 40°。所以在靠近镜面的方向上，`A5` 的衍射光大多落在视野外，看起来就暗。这是粗算，还没有和亮度测量对照过。

如果是这样，带数据的方案就有个具体的风险。字节随机混合后，就不再是一个周期，而是一段较宽的频谱。亮度也许还跟着游程走，也可能因为衍射光散开而差很多。对比盘上的长游程和短游程环正好能分开这两种情况，有结果我贴上来。
以及，目的是存有意义的数据，还是只要能挂载就好？如果是能挂载，我有这样一个iso： > NaiveTomcat通过QQ闪传分享了【dvd_full2.iso】 > 链接：https://qfile.qq.com/q/iU2b5RtDZm 烧出的盘长这样： 具有可以在访达挂载的文件系统：

那果然……

其实不是标靶中的块。是 https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/issues/90#issuecomment-6656446826 ISO里面的。如果是标靶的话，我这边测试直接最开始就读不出。不过这个无所谓，反正重要的是找到一个这样的块。

> 让 DVD 的图案区域同时存数据

想到一块了，在 #90 我就突然想到如果是有多个扰码Q能呈现几乎一样的最终效果，那可以利用此做隐写术。不知道这样能整盘下来存多少数据。

更新：刻好的对比盘第一次读回。平时很少报错的 GH70N，每种纹理读 9 块：把 `92` 强制推进 6T/10T 码字的环 9 块全读不出；普通 `92` 只有 1 块读不出；其他纹理全能读，包括长、短游程字节随机混合的两种。这是第一次只改 `92` 的码字形式就看到读取跟着变，不过只有一张盘、一台光驱。详情在主帖。

另外 `A5` 模型里峰值 325 却读得很好，所以 DSV 峰值单独预测不了，偏多久可能比偏多高更重要。

但这会一定程度上牺牲图案对比度
